We're one of the fastest-growing Shopify Retention Agencies in the space, and the brands we work with love us for it. Our team is small, sharp, and obsessed with turning one-time buyers into loyal customers - and we're looking for someone who shares that obsession, and can lead others toward it too.
We're a remote-first company, so you're free to work whenever suits you best, just make sure you're online from 12–5pm CE(S)T so we can stay in sync with the team and clients. Please only apply if you can commit to this.
Your mission: own the strategy and outcomes for your pod's highest-value, most complex accounts, turning data-driven decisions and strong client leadership into the standard the rest of the team is built to meet.
What you'll do:
1. Independently manage 5-6 Shopify brands doing over 5M/y, including our most complex, highest-value accounts
2. Own the retention roadmap across your portfolio: planning calendars, timing, and revenue targets, and interpreting data to define next steps
3. Develop advanced retention strategies and review campaigns before they reach the client
4. Work with a more junior Retention Manager who handles copy and project management for your clients, freeing you up to focus on strategy and the relationship
5. Mentor RM1s and RM2s in your pod: coach them on client-facing skills, strategic thinking, and data-driven decision-making
6. Run client onboarding for new brands, setting the right tone and expectations from day one
7. Stay genuinely at the cutting edge of retention marketing and bring that thinking back to the team
What we're looking for (non negotiable):
1. 4+ years hands-on experience, including running high-value/high-complexity accounts
2. Full funnel understanding, not just email metrics
3. Proven ability to develop retention strategy from scratch,
4. Strong relationship builder with proven client-facing experience, including coaching or mentoring other marketers
5. Agency background or 8fig+ brand experience
What you'll get:
1. Competitive salary
2. Generous paid time off
3. Fully remote - work from wherever you do your best work
4. Clear growth path into Team Lead and beyond
5. Access to all tools, data, courses and coaches you need for being successful
6. Direct access to founders of the fastest growing e-commerce brands worldwide
This is for you if:
- You're a freelancer/agency owner who wants more stability, without giving up ownership
- You want the hardest, highest-stakes accounts on your desk, not the easy ones
- You like making other people better at their jobs, not just doing your own well
This is not for you if:
- You're looking to get away by doing the bare minimum
- You want to stay heads-down on execution and skip the mentoring/strategy side
Speak soon ❤️ 🔥

JOIN NEUDATA - BUSINESS DEVELOPMENT EXECUTIVE
Introducing Neudata:
Neudata is the global leader in alternative and market data intelligence, helping investors, hedge funds and corporates discover, evaluate, and use data to make smarter decisions. Our independence is what really sets us apart - we provide objective, unbiased intelligence that our clients trust and depend on.
With offices in London, New York, and Shanghai and a team of 100 people, we connect a vast global network of buyers and providers through our market-leading platforms and specialist consulting - and by providing a clear view of the data landscape, we help organisations navigate complexity and find their competitive edge. Joining Neudata really puts you at the heart of the fintech industry, where your work directly influences the data-driven strategies of the world’s most sophisticated organisations.
The Role:
At Neudata, we help data vendors unlock their full potential with our industry-leading Neudata Provider Premium service. We work with data owners to enhance their products and accelerate sales, connecting them with the largest data-buying firms worldwide.
This is a role for someone starting out in sales. We're looking for around one to two years' experience in an office environment, in any field, so this could be your first move into a sales career. You'll learn the market, the product and the sales cycle with close support from the team, and take on more ownership as you go.
As a Business Development Executive, you’ll play a key role in growing our business by:
- Identifying and closing opportunities: Engage prospects, run outreach campaigns, and convert leads into long-term clients
- Building lasting relationships: Manage and maximise the value of your accounts; identifying opportunities to upsell and cross-sell
- Driving revenue growth: Promote our Neudata Provider Premium services and our industry-leading events to new and existing customers
Your Key Responsibilities:
- Pitch and sell our flagship Neudata Provider Premium service, showing data owners exactly how we can accelerate their sales and unlock the full potential of their products
- Champion our high-profile events to the biggest names in data, generating genuine buzz, interest and attendance across the industry
- Design and run outbound campaigns that start conversations, generate quality leads and keep your pipeline flowing
- Take ownership of your own portfolio of accounts, spotting opportunities to upsell and cross-sell while building relationships that genuinely last
- Seek out and win new clients, expanding our reach into new firms and markets across the globe
- Roll up your sleeves for a variety of projects along the way – with us, no two weeks look the same
What You’ll Bring:
- Educated to degree level, with around one to two years' experience in an office environment, in any field. You don't need previous sales experience, and this could be your first sales role
- An entrepreneurial streak and a sharp commercial mindset - you spot opportunities and go after them
- Genuine curiosity about the data economy and the wider business world.
- Fantastic communication and interpersonal skills - you can build rapport with just about anyone
- A love of fast-paced, client-facing work and a real hunger to learn and grow
- A proactive, goal-driven attitude and the determination to deliver results
- Above all, great energy and a genuine desire to learn
Our Benefits & Perks:
- 25 days’ annual leave + bank holidays, plus an extra day for each year of service (up to 30 days), alongside one paid volunteering day and two paid study days per year 📅
- Hybrid and flexible working, including working from anywhere for up to 10 working days per year from a location of your choosing 🌍
- Private medical insurance via Vitality (including dental, optical, and hearing) ✚
- Enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental policies 👨‍👩‍👧‍👦
- Enhanced pension scheme via NEST 📈
- Employee referral bonus of £1,000 per successful new hire you refer 💸
Key Details:
- Location: London (Moorgate)
- Start Date: ASAP
Recruitment Process:
1. Initial screening call with our Talent Acquisition Manager
2. First-stage competency interview
3. Second-stage task & meeting with members of the team
4. Final stage interview
Candidates who may require visa sponsorship should discuss this with the hiring manager during the interview process. Further information on Skilled Worker sponsorship can be found here https://www.gov.uk/skilled-worker-visa/your-job.
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and shortlisted candidates will be invited to an initial screening call with our Talent Acquisition Manager.

JOIN NEUDATA - SALES DIRECTOR (EMEA & ASIA-PACIFIC)
Introducing Neudata:
Neudata is the global leader in alternative and market data intelligence, helping investors, hedge funds and corporates discover, evaluate, and use data to make smarter decisions. Our independence is what really sets us apart - we provide objective, unbiased intelligence that our clients trust and depend on.
With offices in London, New York, and Shanghai and a team of 100 people, we connect a vast global network of buyers and providers through our market-leading platforms and specialist consulting - and by providing a clear view of the data landscape, we help organisations navigate complexity and find their competitive edge. Joining Neudata really puts you at the heart of the fintech industry, where your work directly influences the data-driven strategies of the world's most sophisticated organisations.
The Role:
We're looking for an experienced, entrepreneurial Sales Director to take our Scout and Ranger platforms to data buyers across EMEA and APAC: hedge funds, asset managers, private equity firms and the fast-growing world of AI. This is a pure new business role, and you'll own your territory end to end, from spotting the opportunity through to signing the deal.
Partnering directly with our Chief Revenue Officer, you'll play an important part in refining how we approach the EMEA and APAC data buyer markets, identifying opportunities for growth, developing repeatable sales practices, and laying the foundations for an expanded European sales team.
You'll be the face of Neudata in front of some of the most sophisticated investors in the market, running story-led demonstrations, guiding hands-on trials alongside our research analysts, and building relationships with the people who decide how their firms use external data.
We encourage applications from high-performing Sales Reps looking to take on greater ownership and responsibility in a fast-growing organisation. There is potential for the successful candidate to take on a leadership role over time.
Your Key Responsibilities:
- Own the EMEA and Asia-Pacific territory of institutional investor prospects, driving new business through proactive outreach, travelling to meet prospects in-person, and lead generation campaigns across email and socials
- Run the full sales cycle: leading discovery and qualification calls, delivering value-based, story-led demonstrations of Scout and Ranger, then negotiating commercial terms and closing in line with quota
- Manage hands-on platform trials in partnership with our research analysts, aligning technical and business criteria so prospects can see the value for themselves
- Represent Neudata on stage and on the ground, presenting at our own high-profile events and at external conferences in the UK and overseas
- Become a trusted advisor to senior stakeholders, from Heads of Data and Portfolio Managers through to Procurement Leads
- Work closely with the CRO to develop and execute territory plans, prioritise attractive markets and client segments, and identify opportunities to accelerate growth
- Keep your pipeline sharp with rigorous CRM discipline and accurate forecasting, and feed market insight back to our product and research teams to help shape where we go next
- Contribute to the development of repeatable sales processes, messaging and best practices that can support an expanded European sales team
- As the team expands, contribute to the recruitment, onboarding, coaching and development of new sales colleagues, with scope to take on formal management responsibilities
What You'll Bring:
- Strong experience in data, research or information sales, ideally into financial services, with a proven track record of originating and closing complex new logo deals
- Sharp commercial acumen and the confidence to negotiate and close
- Experience independently developing new territories, market segments and commercial opportunities
- Outstanding presentation and communication skills, in person and online, in front of senior and technical audiences alike
- Familiarity with how investment firms buy, particularly asset managers and hedge funds, and with the stakeholders involved along the way
- Genuine enthusiasm for alternative data, market data and investment research, and curiosity about where the data landscape is heading
- Experience coaching or managing people in a commercial setting is a bonus, but not essential
Our Benefits & Perks:
- 25 days' annual leave + bank holidays, plus an extra day for each year of service (up to 30 days), alongside one paid volunteering day and two paid study days per year 📅
- Hybrid and flexible working, including working from anywhere for up to 10 working days per year from a location of your choosing 🌍
- Private medical insurance via Vitality (including dental, optical, and hearing) ✚
- Enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental policies 🏠
- Enhanced pension scheme via NEST 📈
- Employee referral bonus of £1,000 per successful new hire you refer 💸
Key Details:
- Location: London (Moorgate) with hybrid working. Frequent travel across EMEA and Asia is anticipated.
- Salary: Competitive base salary and commission structure
- Start Date: ASAP
- Line Manager: Chief Revenue Officer
Recruitment Process:
1. Initial screening call with our Talent Acquisition Manager
2. First-stage competency interview
3. Meetings with key Neudata stakeholders
4. Final stage interview
Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and shortlisted candidates will be invited to an initial screening call with our Talent Acquisition Manager.
Applicants must be eligible to work in the UK. Candidates who may require visa sponsorship should discuss this with the hiring manager during the interview process. Further information on Skilled Worker sponsorship can be found here https://www.gov.uk/skilled-worker-visa/your-job.

JOIN NEUDATA - RESEARCH ANALYST
Introducing Neudata:
Neudata is the global leader in alternative and market data intelligence, helping investors, hedge funds and corporates discover, evaluate, and use data to make smarter decisions. Our independence is what really sets us apart - we provide objective, unbiased intelligence that our clients trust and depend on.
Neudata’s research team is at the core of what we do. Clients of Neudata have access to:
- Our research portal, allowing them to browse our catalogue of dataset reports, each of which is written by a member of the research team and pertaining to a dataset (e.g. short positions data by vendor X)
- Our research team’s expertise, allowing us to help them make informed data decisions (e.g. through calls where we share our opinion on the most appropriate dataset for their needs)
The Role:
Our expertise lies in the vast world of alternative data, spanning everything from social sentiment feeds and credit card transactions to complex ESG signals. As a Research Analyst, you will join the team dedicated to Scout, our premier platform for alternative data discovery. You will be largely interacting with:
- Data buyers, by communicating our findings via research reports and calls, and
- Data sellers, to understand their properties and potential use cases of different datasets
Your work will centre on translating complex, non-traditional datasets into actionable intelligence in a highly collaborative and inquisitive role that requires a blend of analytical thinking and clear, authoritative communication.
Your Key Responsibilities:
- Conducting in-depth research on alternative data providers and datasets
- Writing research reports on alternative datasets and industry trends
- Interacting with our client base (data buyers and data sellers), primarily through research calls and emails
- Gathering industry intelligence via effective relationships built through our reputation in the industry
- We highly encourage our Research Analysts to exercise independent thought and critical thinking, and believe this to be one of the most appealing aspects of the role
What You’ll Bring:
- Enthusiasm for data and understand its impact to users in various industries, particularly the financial sector

- You want to become an industry expert in alternative data and have an eagerness to help discover new, under the radar datasets
- Knowledge of the investment management industry/alternative data market is a plus, but not a necessity
- You do not require advanced knowledge or experience in data science - this isn’t a data science role
Our Benefits & Perks:
- 25 days' annual leave + bank holidays, plus an extra day for each year of service (up to 30 days), alongside one paid volunteering day and two paid study days per year 📅
- Hybrid and flexible working, including working from anywhere for up to 10 working days per year from a location of your choosing 🌍
- Private medical insurance via Vitality (including dental, optical, and hearing) ✚
- Enhanced maternity, paternity, adoption and shared parental policies 🏠
- Enhanced pension scheme via NEST 📈
- Employee referral bonus of £1,000 per successful new hire you refer 💸
Key Details:
- Location: London (Moorgate)
- Start Date: ASAP
Recruitment Process:
1. Initial screening call with our Talent Acquisition Manager
2. Competency interview with our Head of Research
3. Written task and meetings with Team Leads
4. Final stage interview & presentation

jobs.ashbyhq.com/nory/702809f7-520b-4cbd.description_excerpt:
Let’s fix hospitality, for good.
Hospitality is tough – margins are thin, waste is high, and teams are stretched. But it doesn’t have to be this hard. That’s why we built Nory.
Our CEO, Conor, knows the pain first-hand. After founding and scaling Mad Egg in Ireland, he got fed up with juggling “market-leading” systems, clunky spreadsheets, and endless printouts. So he set out to build the tool he wished he’d had from day one.
Nory is an all-knowing restaurant management system. It blends real-time data with AI predictive analytics, giving operators control of their margins. From food prep to forecasting, it’s operational intelligence that helps restaurants run with consistency, certainty, and profit. The result? Thriving restaurants, better jobs, less waste, healthier margins.
And we’re just getting started. Fresh off a Series B led by Kinnevik https://www.nory.ai/blog/nory-series-b-funding-to-revolutionise-restaurant-operations, we’ve grown to 100+ people across Ireland, the UK, Spain and New York – and demand is scaling faster than we ever imagined.
THE ROLE:
We're looking for a UK & US Payroll Processor to join our growing Payroll team on a 6-month contract, with the potential to become permanent. You'll make sure our hospitality clients get accurate, on-time payroll and deliver clear support through our payroll inbox.
You'll mainly process UK and US payroll. It's a fantastic opportunity to help us launch into the US market.
Hours: UK business hours
WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:
- Payroll Processing: Prepare and process payroll for hospitality businesses, ensuring accuracy and compliance with UK payroll legislation.
- Payroll Inbox: Manage and respond to queries from employees and clients via the payroll inbox, covering pay calculations, tax deductions, pension contributions, and related matters.
- Compliance: Ensure all processing is carried out in line with current UK payroll legislation and statutory requirements.
- Record Keeping: Maintain accurate and up-to-date payroll records for each client.
- Escalation: Identify and escalate more complex payroll queries to senior team members where needed.
- Ad Hoc Support: Assist with other payroll tasks and projects as required.
WHAT YOU’LL BRING:
Essential:
- Hands-on UK payroll processing experience, with strong knowledge of UK payroll legislation and compliance (PAYE, RTI, auto-enrolment, SSP/SMP).
- Experience using payroll software or platforms.
- Understanding of tax codes, National Insurance, pensions, and statutory payments.
- High attention to detail and accuracy in payroll processing.
- Strong numerical and analytical skills.
- Proficiency in Microsoft Excel or Google Sheets for payroll reporting.
- Excellent communication skills, with the ability to explain payroll matters clearly to both clients and employees.
- Ability to work efficiently in a fast-paced, deadline-driven environment.
- Able to work UK business hours.
Desirable:
- Experience processing US payroll (federal and state tax, multi-state employees, US payroll providers).
- Experience with Ireland payroll legislation (PAYE, USC, PRSI).
- Knowledge of HR and workforce management software.
- Experience working in a SaaS (Software as a Service) environment.
If you’re excited by what we’re building, we’d love to hear from you, even if you don’t tick every box.
WHAT YOU’LL GET IN RETURN:
💰 Competitive rate depending on experience
📈 Meaningful equity, at Nory everyone is an owner!
🌴 35 days of paid leave per year (including bank holidays)
🏥 Comprehensive private health insurance via Irish Life (Ireland) and Axa (UK)
🍼 Enhanced parental leave and baby loss support
📚 Learning & development culture – €1000 personal annual budget + quarterly book budget
🖥️ €250 home office workspace budget
🥳 Regular team offsites & socials
🌎 Work from anywhere for up to 3 months of the year
📍Offices in either London 🇬🇧 , Dublin 🇮🇪 or Spain 🇪🇸
👏 And much more
HOW WE WORK
Our vision is to build a better future for the restaurant industry.
One where operators are in control, margins are stronger, and frontline teams can build careers they’re proud of. To get there, we move fast, stay focused, and hold ourselves to a high bar. Our values guide how we work, grow, and win – together.
These are the values we live by:
We serve up impact with a side of profit: We prioritise work that delivers real financial results for our restaurant partners.
We prioritise speed of service: We move fast, unblock quickly, and deliver with urgency.
We act like owners: We own problems, raise the bar, and build better every day.
We win as a crew: We grow stronger through feedback, collaboration, and shared wins.
WE HIRE HUMANS.
At Nory, we believe that diverse teams build better products. We welcome applicants from all backgrounds, identities, and walks of life. We do not discriminate based on gender, ethnicity, sexual orientation, religion, family status, age, disability, or race. What matters to us is how you think, how you work, and what you bring to the table. Please let us know if you require any adjustments so you can bring your best self to the interview process.

Hospitality is tough – margins are thin, waste is high, and teams are stretched. But it doesn’t have to be this hard. That’s why we built Nory.
Our CEO, Conor, knows the pain first-hand. After founding and scaling Mad Egg in Ireland, he got fed up with juggling “market-leading” systems, clunky spreadsheets, and endless printouts. So he set out to build the tool he wished he’d had from day one.
Nory is an all-knowing restaurant management system. It blends real-time data with AI predictive analytics, giving operators control of their margins. From food prep to forecasting, it’s operational intelligence that helps restaurants run with consistency, certainty, and profit. The result? Thriving restaurants, better jobs, less waste, healthier margins.

THE ROLE:
We’re now looking for an FP&A Lead to join our growing Finance and Operations team. In this role, you’ll have the unique opportunity to own and build Nory’s FP&A function end-to-end, turning our plans and numbers into the decisions that power our next stage of growth.
WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING:
- Own the planning cycle: Lead the annual budget, reforecasts and long-range plan, from building the model through to sign-off with the exec team and board.
- Run performance reporting: Deliver clear, timely monthly management reporting and board packs, with commentary that explains what happened, why, and what we should do next.
- Partner with the business: Work with leaders across Sales, Marketing, Customer Success, People, Product and Engineering to set targets, track KPIs and make smart trade-offs on headcount and spend.
- Own the metrics that matter: Be the source of truth for our core SaaS metrics (ARR, net revenue retention, CAC payback, burn and runway) so everyone trusts the numbers.
- Support the big decisions: Build the models and analysis behind fundraising, pricing, new-market expansion and other strategic bets.
- Scale the function: Improve our tools, data and processes so FP&A keeps pace as Nory grows, and help shape the team over time.
You’ll report to a finance leader with a deep FP&A background who’ll be a sounding board and strong support, but this is your function to drive.
WHAT YOU’LL BRING:
- FP&A depth: 6+ years in FP&A or strategic finance, ideally including time in a high-growth SaaS or tech business. A professional accounting qualification is not required but you do need to know accounting principles and be able to create solid three-statement forecasts.
- End-to-end ownership: You’ve run budgeting, forecasting and reporting cycles yourself, not just contributed to them.
- Strong modelling skills: You build driver-based and three-statement models that are robust, flexible and easy for others to follow. Excel / Google sheets are a must, SQL and other tools are desirable.
- Commercial judgement: You go beyond the numbers, form a clear point of view and influence senior stakeholders.
- Clear communication: You explain complex financials simply, whether you’re talking to a team lead or the board.
- Startup mindset: You thrive in fast-paced environments, move quickly and are comfortable with ambiguity. You’d rather ship a good-enough forecast today than a perfect one next month.
- Drive to build: You’ve created and improved scalable finance processes and tools, and you think long-term about how the function should grow. .

Money stress is the biggest productivity killer in the workplace - My Money Matters exists to change that. We're building an app that improves employees' finances automatically every pay day - giving them financial tools that directly improve their financial health with less effort.
Every pay day is an opportunity to build better money habits. We make it easy. Employees can accelerate retirement savings with tax-efficient pension top-ups, build a safety net effortlessly with auto savings, or access their already-earned salary ahead of pay day for emergencies.
For employers, fewer employees with money worries means more focus on work. We're trusted by major organisations including the NHS, and we're growing fast.
Role Overview
As a Customer Launch Manager in our Launch team, you lead customer onboarding from contract signature to go-live. You take over from Sales and get each new customer live in under 30 days, with as many employees signed up as possible from day one.
You own the journey from signature to launch: set-up, payroll and data readiness, employer communications and the pre-launch sign-up drive. Speed and take-up are what matter. A fast launch means our customers see value sooner, and every employee signed up at launch is revenue from day one.
Once the customer is live, you hand over to the Account Manager, so they pick up a live, well-understood account that is ready to grow.
The role is hybrid, with 1-2 days in the London office per week.
Key Responsibilities
Handover from Sales
- Take a structured handover from Sales at contract signature, confirming scope, products, key contacts and launch date
- Support Sales on late-stage deals where needed, so what is sold can be launched quickly
- Run a kick-off with the employer within the first week and agree a launch plan with clear owners and dates
Launch in Under 30 Days
- Own each launch end to end, from kick-off to go-live, for a portfolio of new customers
- Build out a mutually agreed launch plan with the customer
- Get payroll, data and integrations ready, working through requirements, testing and sign-off with the employer
- Spot risks, dependencies and blockers early and remove them before they slip the date
- Keep launches consistent and repeatable, using standard playbooks and adapting only where the customer needs it
Sign-ups Ready for Launch
- Own a pre-launch sign-up target for every launch
- Plan employee communications with the employer and Marketing: announcements, webinars, pay-slip messages and on-site sessions
- Equip HR, Payroll and line managers to promote the service
- Track sign-ups against target in the run-up to launch and act quickly where take-up is low
Handover to Account Management
- Hand each live customer to the Account Manager with a clear record of scope, stakeholders, sign-ups and next opportunities
- Run launches of new products for existing customers when the Account Manager closes an expansion
Cross-Functional Collaboration
- Sales: feedback on what speeds up or slows down launch, so deals are shaped to launch well
- Marketing: launch campaigns and sign-up materials
- Product and Engineering: raise blockers early and feedback on set-up friction
- Improve the launch playbook, documentation and ways of working over time
How Success Is Measured
Speed and take-up come first; quality of handover protects both.
Measure
What it shows
Time to launch
Days from contract signature to go-live, against a 30-day target
Sign-ups at launch
Employees signed up by go-live, against target
Launch take-up rate
Share of eligible employees signed up by go-live
Launches on time
Share of launches delivered on the agreed date
Handover quality
Account Manager and customer feedback on the handover
Skills & Competencies
Core Skills
- Strong delivery and coordination: runs several launches in parallel and hits dates (formal project management background not required)
- Pace and urgency: removes blockers rather than waiting for them to clear
- Confident with payroll, data and integration requirements, and able to lead those conversations with customers
- Campaign mindset: knows how to drive employee take-up through clear, well-timed communications
- Communicates clearly with technical and non-technical stakeholders, from payroll teams to HR directors
- Takes ownership of outcomes, not just activity, with minimal day-to-day direction
Experience & Background
- Proven track record delivering customer onboarding, implementation or launches in a SaaS or platform business
- Experience driving user or employee adoption, ideally in employee benefits, payroll, HR or financial wellbeing
- Experience managing several customer projects at once against tight timelines
- Experience with payroll data, integrations or HR systems is advantageous
- Experience with public sector or other complex organisations is advantageous but not essential
What the Role Is Not
- A reactive technical support role
- A back-office set-up role: launch success is measured by sign-ups, not just go-live
- A long-term account role: once a customer is live, the Account Manager takes over
- A role requiring task-level direction
This role suits someone who loves pace and ownership and wants to see every launch go live quickly with employees signed up and ready to benefit.

Stage 2 | Hiring Manager Interview – A 60-minute interview with the Hiring Manager to explore your experience in more detail, your approach to the role and give you the opportunity to learn more about the team and what we’re building.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/namespace/c31e067e-f10d.description_excerpt:
JOIN OUR MISSION
We're proud to work with many incredible companies, accelerating their ability to build their products.
We've spent years watching talented engineering teams lose momentum to the same frustrating bottleneck: waiting. Waiting for CI to finish. Waiting for builds to complete. Waiting for tests to run.
After experiencing this pain firsthand at companies of every size, we set out to build the developer infrastructure platform we'd always wanted to use. Something that would seamlessly integrate with our workflows and the tools teams already love—but make everything dramatically faster and more cost-effective.
Today, we're already accelerating hundreds of companies around the world, helping them ship features instead of waiting for infrastructure. We've built something that feels almost magical in its simplicity: change your runs-on line, mount your toolchain cache directory and suddenly your builds are 5x faster.
ABOUT THE ROLE
Namespace's approach is low-friction, designed for immediate integration into existing developer toolchains, empowering teams to experience tangible results within just five minutes. With an end-to-end stack optimized for high performance—including compute, memory, storage, and networking—Namespace delivers capabilities and efficiencies unmatched by traditional cloud providers.
As a Product Engineer at Namespace, you'll develop products that significantly enhance developer productivity. You'll build intuitive, performant user-facing applications and integrations that seamlessly fit into developers' existing workflows, directly impacting their ability to ship faster and more efficiently.
OUR CULTURE
We're looking for people with grit—people who push through ambiguity, take ownership, and keep going when things get hard. You're deeply curious, driven to understand how things work and how they can be improved. Most importantly, you have a strong bias to execution: you don't wait for perfect conditions, you ship, learn, and iterate quickly. If you care about building, moving fast, and making real impact, you'll fit right in.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Own and ship end-to-end features that integrate seamlessly with popular developer tools
- Develop user-facing applications that make powerful infrastructure intuitive and accessible to developers
- Collaborate directly with users and partners to deeply understand their workflows, pain points, and product needs
- Continuously iterate on product design and implementation to drive adoption, performance, and reliability
WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- Strong software engineering fundamentals, with experience building production-grade software in languages like TypeScript/JavaScript (React), Go, Python, or similar
- Proven track record shipping impactful product features, preferably for developer-focused or infrastructure products
- Customer-centric mindset with the ability to translate complex technical solutions into intuitive user experiences
- Enthusiasm for continuous learning and a collaborative approach to product development
You can expect:
- Competitive salary and stock options
- Flexible working hours
- Market-leading parental leave
Life at Namespace Labs:
- We pride ourselves in being a small team of experts that can achieve a lot.
- We balance our long-term vision with short-term pragmatism.
- We believe in being fully transparent internally on how decisions are made, on how the company is doing, and we use that information to drive our decisions.

We power card issuing for leading banks, fintechs and digital brands across the globe, and as we continue to grow, we are looking for curious, ambitious people who thrive on solving complex challenges, embrace innovation and want to make a tangible impact at global scale.
Role Purpose
The Financial Accountant is responsible for the end-to-end financial accounting and compliance activities for a few markets. This role ensures accurate and timely month-end close, statutory and tax compliance, audit support, balance sheet integrity, and financial reporting. The position works closely with Commercial Finance, Payroll, Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Tax, and external advisors to deliver high-quality financial information, drive process improvements, and support business decision-making.
Key Responsibilities
Financial Close & Reporting
· Lead the month-end, quarter-end, and year-end close processes for assigned markets, ensuring accurate and timely financial reporting.
· Prepare and post journal entries, accruals, prepayments, and other accounting adjustments.
· Review and analyse profit and loss accounts and balance sheet movements.
· Ensure compliance with group accounting policies and local statutory requirements.

About Pikl
Pikl is on a mission to enable the growth of digital marketplaces, starting with vacation rentals. We design and deliver insurance-enabled solutions that help platforms, property managers and owners unlock new revenue and deliver better customer experiences.
Launched in 2019, we began by protecting individual hosts and homeowners with specialist holiday-let cover. That experience now powers our insurance-enabled products, which increase participation, lift conversion and drive revenue across the marketplace value chain: platforms, homeowners and guests.
With offices in Norwich and London, and plans for international expansion, we work with some of the most recognised brands in travel as well as major insurance aggregators.
About the role
The IT Manager is responsible for the secure, reliable and efficient operation of Pikl’s IT environment, supporting colleagues primarily in Norwich, London and working from home. This role sits at the intersection of IT operations and information security, combining hands-on support, infrastructure oversight and vendor management with accountability for delivering secure and well-governed systems.
Working closely with our external IT provider and CISO, the IT Manager ensures that systems, controls and processes are not only well designed but consistently executed. This role is less about owning strategy and more about high-quality delivery, operational discipline, and continuous improvement across IT and security.
The role also plays a key part in enabling the safe adoption of AI tools across the business, ensuring appropriate controls, guardrails and infrastructure are in place.
Key Responsibilities
IT Operations & Infrastructure
- Act as the primary IT contact, providing responsive, high-quality support for end users
- Maintain the day-to-day operation of IT infrastructure including endpoints, networks, Wi-Fi and core cloud systems
- Manage joiner and leaver processes from an IT perspective, ensuring consistent, secure provisioning and deprovisioning
- Own and maintain the IT asset register, including procurement, tracking and lifecycle management
- Maintain office technology and audio-visual equipment to a high and reliable standard
- Deliver small-to-medium IT improvements and projects
- Act as the interface with the external IT provider, managing tickets, prioritisation and service quality
- Maintain clear, structured documentation for systems, processes and controls to support resilience and audit readiness
- Drive measurable improvements in system reliability, security posture and user experience
- Manage supplier relationships to ensure value for money and reliable service
Information Security
- Implement and operate security controls
- Administer core security tooling (endpoint protection, email security, identity and access management, patching)
- Support user access control, device compliance and secure configuration standards
- Deliver day-to-day security activities including patching, monitoring and basic incident triage
- Support and maintain backup and disaster recovery processes, ensuring data is protected and recoverable
- Support audits, supplier due diligence and compliance activities (e.g. Cyber Essentials, ISO 27001)
- Promote good security practices across the business through practical guidance and user support
- Escalate risks, incidents and control gaps clearly and promptly
AI & Tooling Enablement
- Support rollout and safe usage of approved AI tools ensuring controls are followed
- Enforce policies around data handling and access when using AI-enabled platforms
- Ensure devices, identity and monitoring environments are configured to support safe AI adoption
- Provide practical guidance to colleagues on appropriate use of AI tools in their work
Governance & Performance
- Maintain clear, structured documentation for systems, processes and controls to support resilience and audit readiness
- Monitor system performance and proactively resolve issues before they escalate
- Support IT budgeting processes through accurate tracking of spend and asset planning
- Drive measurable improvements in system reliability, security posture and user experience
- Provide clear operational insight to leadership on performance, risks and recurring issues
About you
- Significant experience in an IT support, or IT manager role
- Strong working knowledge of Microsoft 365 and modern endpoint management
- Comfortable owning day-to-day IT operations in a small-to-mid sized business environment
- Experience working with an outsourced IT provider, with the ability to manage and challenge constructively
- Solid understanding of networking basics (Wi-Fi, routing, connectivity troubleshooting)
- Hands-on experience supporting end users, devices and office-based IT environments
- Practical experience implementing security controls and tooling
- Awareness of Cyber Essentials / ISO 27001 style controls and how they apply operationally
- Implementation of ISO 27001 or ISO27k1 would be an advantage
- Exposure to AI tools in a workplace context and an understanding of associated risks
- Highly organised, with strong attention to detail and good documentation habits
- Clear communicator, able to explain technical issues in a straightforward, pragmatic way
- Comfortable working independently and taking ownership of outcomes
Our Values
At Pikl, our values are the foundation on which our success is built. They guide how we work together, how we make decisions for customers and colleagues, and what we recognise and reward.
Possibility
We think big and are fearless in turning challenges into opportunities. We stay curious, test ideas and learn quickly.
People
We put people first, building relationships rooted in empathy and trust. We respect, include, and learn from one another. We celebrate progress.
Progress
We unlock growth opportunities for our customers and each other yet make it our personal responsibility to own actions and see them through.

- Access to an incredible working space in Norwich and London

Plain is redefining customer support for the next generation of B2B companies. We’re building the fastest, most powerful platform to help companies move beyond reactive support and build true customer relationships.
Some of the world’s most forward-thinking companies - like Cursor, Raycast, and Granola - trust Plain to unify all customer interactions, enable faster team collaboration, and supercharge their workflows with AI.
B2B customer support is undergoing a seismic shift. AI is transforming the way companies engage with customers, shifting support from a siloed function to a company-wide effort across Slack, Discord, and any other channel you talk to customers in. The old way - slow, manual, and disconnected - no longer works.
This role is hybrid with 3 days a week in our London office.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Engineering at Plain is about much more than moving tickets from left to right - it’s about owning and solving problems end to end, from infrastructure decisions to feature design to button copy.
You will:
- Help set product direction. You’ll contribute to both the technical architecture and the roadmap, balancing customer feedback with long-term product health.
- Ship features end to end. You’ll scope, build, and launch product features that directly solve customer problems. We’re structured into the following teams right now:
- Core Product: Own all customer-facing channels (Slack, Discord, Email, etc), core data models, and customer requests. You’ll balance moving fast to win customers with investing in strong foundations for the future.
- Developer Infra: Build the tools that every engineer at Plain depends on to ship and operate the product. Your focus is on making the team faster, removing roadblocks before they happen, and ensuring everything we build is easy to run, debug, and control in production.
- Shape our backend architecture. You’ll tackle some of our most complex challenges, from data modeling to high-performance reporting, and help set the standard for how we build across the company.
- Create a stellar developer experience. From data pipelines to APIs, you’ll make sure Plain is not only great to use but also great to build on.
THIS IS A GREAT FIT IF YOU…
- Thrive in early ideation stages, love sharing work-in-progress, and enjoy the balance of making trade-offs in order to ship high impact products.
- Are impact driven and motivated by seeing customers succeed. You measure the quality of your work by the end-experience of users, not the abstractions or cleanliness of the code.
- Have a proven track record working for product-led companies, ideally in B2B SaaS.
- You’re autonomous and able to prioritise your workload. You know when to take a shortcut and when to invest in long-term infrastructure.
- Have experience working with distributed, serverless systems, and have worked on similar web applications with a high quality and performance bar before
- Are equally at home in architectural conversations as you are in customer conversations.
- Can learn new technologies and paradigms quickly and independently.
THIS WON'T BE THE RIGHT ROLE IF YOU…
- Are uncomfortable with ambiguity. We have some really exciting traction but are still at an early stage and are constantly learning and trying new things as our company grows.
- Find learning about new technologies a key motivation for coming to work. We invest in what makes us productive but will prefer the known option to the experimental and novel. Postgres is great.
- Are looking to manage others. We're firmly looking for someone who, for now, wants to be an individual contributor.
- Expect all the perks of a big company. We’re a Series A startup and are competitive in what we offer at our stage, but it’s a different role and opportunity than working at an established tech company.

PRACTICE LEAD: AWS
The Practice Lead for AWS is a hands-on leader dedicated to helping customers get the most out of open-source databases running on AWS and the broader AWS ecosystem around them (EKS, Aurora, RDS, ElastiCache, MSK, and the like). While the primary focus is on database environments, the Lead provides architectural guidance across the surrounding infrastructure whenever it affects database performance, cost, or reliability.
As a recognized thought leader, the Practice Lead stays at the forefront of how the AWS platform is evolving, offering strategic advice and direct assistance with complex implementations and migrations.
This is a dedicated, AWS-specific role. We may stand up equivalent practices for other hyperscalers (Azure, GCP) down the road, but for now, the scope is intentionally focused on AWS, and we want deep, real expertise in that ecosystem rather than shallow coverage across three clouds at once.
Our Philosophy: Meet the Customer Where They Are
This role is built around a simple idea: we meet customers where they are, and for a large and growing number of them, that's AWS. The Practice Lead should default to AWS solutions wherever they're the natural, appropriate fit for the customer, and be genuinely enthusiastic about it, not begrudgingly supportive of it. At the same time, "natural fit" is doing real work in that sentence. If a fully managed AWS service isn't the right call for a given customer's cost, portability, or technical requirements, the Practice Lead should say so plainly and recommend the better path, even if that path runs through self-managed or Percona-supported open-source instead.
The job isn't to force AWS onto customers who don't need it, and it isn't to steer people away from AWS out of some reflexive preference for open source either. It's to give customers a straight, technically grounded recommendation and let the right answer win. That's our value of putting the customer ahead of Percona, in practice.
Key Responsibilities
- Customer Advocacy: Act in the best interest of the customer. You will champion Percona's expertise and, where it fits, Percona software and services, but the customer's outcome always comes first, regardless of which tools or platform features get them there.
- Existing Customer Growth: This role isn't just about net-new logos. A meaningful part of the job is looking after Percona's existing customer base as it relates to AWS, in two directions. First, customers already running in AWS environments today: helping them get more value out of that setup, whether that's performance tuning, cost optimization, or adopting additional AWS or Percona services they aren't using yet. Second, customers who aren't on AWS today but are actively migrating there: making sure that transition goes smoothly, that Percona's support and services move with them, and that we don't lose ground with a customer just because their infrastructure is changing.
- Product & Partnership Influence: Act as a strategic advisor to internal Percona teams to improve our software and services for customers running on AWS. You will work closely with our internal Cloud Partnership team on our formal relationship with AWS (co-sell motions, partner programs, joint go-to-market), while you own the technical depth and credibility that makes that partnership valuable in the first place.
- Business Growth: This is a results-oriented role. Success is measured by the revenue and profitability of the AWS Practice, its contribution to Percona subscriptions (Support, Managed Services, etc.), partnership revenue, and overall customer satisfaction.
- Thought Leadership: Drive Percona's presence in the AWS and open source database space through content creation, professional networking, and speaking engagements at industry conferences and AWS-specific events (re:Invent and the like).
- Service Design: Architect professional service offerings and packages, such as migration assessments, cost optimization reviews, and architecture audits, designed for high market impact and successful customer adoption.
- Sales & Marketing Enablement: Serve as a "Super Expert" Solutions Architect during pre-sales cycles. You will work closely with Marketing on technical campaigns and enable the Sales team to win deals with significant AWS components.
- Practice Building: As the business scales, you will be responsible for hiring and mentoring a dedicated team to expand the AWS Practice.
What we are looking for
- AWS expertise: Deep knowledge of AWS and its database ecosystem, including relevant managed services and the infrastructure surrounding them. You understand the trade-offs between managed and self-managed solutions and can make recommendations based on customer needs.
- Open-source database expertise: Strong understanding of open-source database technologies, including MySQL, PostgreSQL, MariaDB and Valkey, with experience helping organisations deploy, optimise and scale these technologies in cloud environments such as AWS.
- Practice-building experience: A track record of building and scaling a consulting, services or technology practice, ideally with responsibility for commercial performance, revenue and profitability.
- Entrepreneurial mindset: Strong work ethic, initiative and a willingness to get hands-on. You’re comfortable building something from the ground up while balancing strategic priorities with day-to-day execution.
- Customer and commercial focus: The ability to build trusted customer relationships, identify growth opportunities and translate technical expertise into tangible business value.
- Strategic thinking and execution: Able to develop a clear vision, turn it into actionable plans and deliver measurable results.
- Communication and influence: An effective communicator who can explain complex technical concepts clearly to both technical and non-technical audiences, build stakeholder confidence and remain composed under pressure. Fluent in written and spoken English.
- Community and thought leadership: A recognised contributor or emerging thought leader in the open-source database or wider cloud ecosystem.
- Sales and business development: Experience supporting technical pre-sales, software sales or business development is desirable but not essential.
- Remote working and travel: Comfortable working in a remote-first environment and travelling

Note: Partly is headquartered in Austin, TX with offices in London, UK, Christchurch, NZ and Auckland, NZ. Wherever you're based, we'll connect you with your nearest office for onboarding, and fly you to join the full team for our quarterly "Season Openers" (we cover travel and accommodation). If you're relocating to join us, we can also assist with relocation costs.
🚀 OUR STORY
Partly is building the infrastructure for anyone to repair anything. We believe everything built should be repairable, and we're building frontier AI to put repair knowledge to work, starting with the $2tn automotive market.
Our model, Interpreter, is the first AI purpose-built to understand repair. Trained on 1M+ car models and 1B+ parts, it reads a repair job the way an estimator does, resolves damage into the exact purchasable part, and shows its reasoning with a confidence score. On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. It powers PartlyRepair, used by collision shops, workshops and suppliers to take the admin off the job; PartlyLabs, the agentic infrastructure enterprises use to deploy Interpreter across their own workflows; and a developer API.
Founded by ex-Rocket Lab engineers, we've raised a $50m Series B led by DST Global (Anthropic, Airbnb, Meta, TikTok, Spotify), with Blackbird Ventures, WNDR, Activant Capital, Icehouse Ventures, Square Peg, Airtree and Ecliptic Venture Capital. Hear it from the team: Why Partly exists https://www.partly.com/nz/careers/videos/why-partly-exists and AI at Partly https://www.partly.com/nz/careers/videos/ai-at-partly.
🖍️ THIS ROLE
As the first time was a huge success, we're launching version 2 of Partly's Repairer Ambassador Programme — a 3-month, full-time (with flexibility), paid internship for a small cohort of sharp, driven graduates who want real responsibility from day one. This is for people who want something more than a coffee run and a PowerPoint, and will lead to a full-time role for those who make a genuine impact.
Your job is simple: get newly onboarded repair shops actively using the Partly platform as quickly as possible. That means building relationships on the ground, understanding why certain shops aren't placing orders through us, and removing those barriers. You'll become the human face of Partly in repair shops across the UK — someone repairers genuinely trust and enjoy working with.
This is not a desk job. You'll spend your first 1–2 weeks in our London office receiving structured training before heading out to visit customers across your assigned region.
Key details:
- Contract: 3 months, full-time with flexibility
- Start: As soon as possible - November 2026
- Location: UK-wide (field-based, with initial training in London)
💻 WHAT WILL YOU DO
- Visit newly signed repair shops across your region and help them get up and running on the Partly platform.
- Understand why shops aren't placing jobs through Partly and identify practical ways to remove those barriers.
- Help repairers optimise and streamline their parts procurement workflows.
- Track repairer activity, monitor adoption, and report insights back to the team on what's working and what isn't.
- Build authentic, long-term relationships with shop owners and parts managers.
- Feed customer insights back to the wider business so we can continually improve the product and onboarding experience.
🥷 WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR
- A recent graduate (university, HND, engineering course, or apprenticeship) with a genuine hunger to learn and get stuck in.
- Strong common sense and the ability to read a room. This role is all about building trust with people who work with their hands for a living.
- A full UK driving licence (having your own car is a strong advantage).
- Comfortable spending most of the week on the road visiting customers.
- Organised, self-directed, and confident working independently.
- Comfortable around automotive professionals. This could come from a genuine interest in cars, working on your own vehicle, following motorsport, spending time in automotive environments, or simply having the curiosity and confidence to quickly learn the industry's language and "talk shop" with customers.
🪅 WHAT YOU’LL GET
- £102 per day
- Travel and accommodation costs covered
- Real responsibility and customer-facing experience from week one
- A strong reference and genuine insight into how a fast-growing tech company operates
- A realistic path to a full-time role at Partly at the end of the programme for the people who excel

On real production jobs, an estimator working with Interpreter reaches 98.8% parts-list accuracy, against 92.1% with today's tools. ABOUT SHARE
Share is a venture-backed startup building the global marketplace for bandwidth. We enable anyone to build their own programmable internet network, in seconds. Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. Only the largest tech companies have escaped this, by spending billions to build their own physical networks. Share is giving that power to everyone.
Infrastructure providers sell their services in the Share Marketplace; giving builders, AI agents and enterprises the ability to build their own global backbone via an API layer. The path, the performance, how long they need it and paying only for what they use.
THE ROLE
We are hiring a Founding Engineer to take ownership of core platform architecture as we rebuild for a system roughly 50x the scale of what we had before. You'll design and scale distributed systems from scratch (this is deep systems-architecture work, not feature development on an existing system.) You will work directly with the Head of Development and a small team of engineers to ship production systems operating at global scale.
Non-negotiable
- 10+ years of professional software engineering experience, with real, hands-on ownership of designing and scaling a production system from scratch. You can describe specific production incidents at scale (what broke, why, and what you changed) not just system-design-interview theory.
- Deep TypeScript/Node.js expertise. You should be able to design a NestJS microservice from scratch, not just work in one.
- Strong PostgreSQL skills. You can design schemas for complex, high-throughput production data, write migrations, and reason about transaction isolation and locking.
- Experience with event-driven architectures (Kafka, RabbitMQ, or similar). You understand the difference between request-reply and fire-and-forget patterns and when to use each.
- You ship. You can take a spec document and turn it into production code without waiting for someone to break it into small tasks.
Nice to have, not required: prior fintech/payments experience or blockchain/distributed-ledger exposure
AI-AUGMENTED ENGINEERING (REQUIRED MINDSET)
We expect every engineer at Share to use AI tools as a daily part of their workflow. This is how we operate. Our entire project planning, specification, and documentation process runs through AI-assisted sessions. Our codebase includes AI-readable context files. We use Claude for architecture decisions, code review, spec generation, and technical writing.
What this means for you:
- You already use AI coding assistants (Claude, Cursor, Copilot, or similar) daily and can articulate how they change your workflow.
- You are comfortable working with AI-generated specifications and can critically evaluate them, push back where they are wrong, and extend them where they are incomplete.
- You see AI as a force multiplier that lets a small team operate at the capacity of a much larger one. You are not threatened by it; you are faster because of it.
- You are willing to contribute to improving our AI-assisted workflows
COMPENSATION & DETAILS:
- Competitive Salary & Equity package
- Additional Benefits
- Paid Business Travel when needed
- Ownership in a venture-backed early stage startup building the future of physical and digital infrastructure in Africa

About Share
Share is a venture-backed startup building the global marketplace for bandwidth. We enable anyone to build their own programmable internet network, in seconds. Today, bandwidth is bought and sold through slow, private, one-off deals, with almost no price transparency. Only the largest tech companies have escaped this, by spending billions to build their own physical networks. Share is giving that power to everyone.
Infrastructure providers sell their services in the Share Marketplace, giving builders, AI agents and enterprises the ability to build their own global backbone via an API layer: the path, the performance, how long they need it, and paying only for what they use.
What you'll do
1. Own our Kubernetes platform end to end. Design, run and scale multi-region clusters and the cloud infrastructure underneath them, mostly on GCP. We target 99.99% availability, and trading on the platform depends on low latency.
2. Run the full stack, old and new: virtual machines in our own data centers, containers and orchestration in the cloud, and everything that connects them.
3. Manage infrastructure as code with Terraform, CI/CD and GitOps, so every change gets reviewed, tested and rolled back like any other code.
4. Build and run the APIs and internal tools the rest of the team builds on, so our software engineers can ship without waiting on anyone.
5. Own monitoring and alerting across the platform with Grafana, Prometheus and OpenTelemetry. Catch degradation before it turns into an incident, and when something does break, lead a blameless post-mortem and make sure the fix lands in the system.
6. Plan capacity and cost as traffic grows, and make the calls on IAM, cloud networking and multi-region design.
7. Work alongside our systems engineer and closely with the network and software teams, and raise the bar for how the whole infrastructure team works.
What we're looking for
1. At least 7 years in platform engineering, SRE or infrastructure, with production systems you were responsible for.
2. Production Kubernetes under real load: deploying it, scaling it, hardening it, and debugging it when it misbehaves.
3. Strong cloud experience, GCP preferred: networking, IAM, cost and capacity planning, multi-region architecture.
4. Depth on both sides of the stack: production Docker and container orchestration, and virtualization (VMware, KVM, Hyper-V or similar). You're as comfortable at the VM layer as you are in a Helm chart.
5. Real API design experience. You've designed, versioned and run APIs that other engineers depended on in production.
6. Terraform, plus CI/CD and GitOps tools like ArgoCD and GitHub Actions.
7. Enough networking to hold your own with our network team: IP routing, VPCs, DNS and load balancing.
8. AI tools as part of how you work, whether that's writing code, automating ops or digging through an outage. We'd like to hear what's helped and what hasn't.
9. You lead without needing the title. You take responsibility for outcomes, argue for the better design when a quick fix is tempting, and use what you learn to push the team forward.
Compensation & Benefits
Competitive salary (top of the local market where you are located) and meaningful equity in a mission-driven, investor-backed company A high-ownership environment with a steep but well-supported learning curve, and a team that writes things down.

Infrastructure providers sell their services in the Share Marketplace; giving builders, AI agents and enterprises the ability to build their own global backbone via an API layer. The path, the performance, how long they need it and paying only for what they use.
The Role
Our network is the foundation of the product. Every route a customer provisions through our API has to exist, perform and stay up on real hardware. We're hiring a Senior Network Developer to design and build that network as software: a distributed, multi-provider fabric that engineers change through code, not by logging into devices.
You'll own the network architecture end to end. That covers our BGP edge (transit, peering at KIXP and LINX, private interconnects with hyperscalers), the backbone, and the PoPs and data centers we're adding across the continent. You'll set the standards our network is built to, which partner ISPs connecting to us will inherit. As we grow, you'll also help build the network engineering team.
What you'll do
- Design the backbone and PoP architecture as standard, repeatable building blocks, from edge to data center, so we can add capacity and new markets without redesigning each time.
- Drive our move to Segment Routing and a clean IP architecture, including IPv4 reuse, IPv6, and how customer and internal address space coexist.
- Build on disaggregated white-box hardware (Edgecore with IP Infusion OcNOS today), and make the hardware and software calls that keep us fast and affordable.
- Turn operations into software. That means a source of truth (Nautobot), templated config (Jinja), and CI/CD with validation, staged rollouts and rollback for every change.
- Build the telemetry and observability that show what the network is really doing. Use AI where it actually helps: anomaly detection, automated triage, and auto-remediation with a human in the loop.
- Own availability. Limit how much any failure can affect, mitigate first and diagnose second, and turn post-mortems into fixes in the system.
- Work with our software team on the API and provisioning layer that exposes the network to customers, and with partner ISPs' engineers on the hand-off.
- Help hire and develop the engineers who'll run this with you.
Our Ideal Candidate
- 8+ years building and operating large networks at a hyperscaler, CDN, internet exchange, carrier or ISP.
- Deep BGP at scale: route policy, communities, RPKI, traffic engineering, peering and transit.
- Strong data center and backbone design. You know Clos/EVPN-VXLAN fabrics and MPLS or Segment Routing, and when each makes sense.
- Hands-on with white-box or disaggregated networking, including choosing hardware and knowing where the silicon limits you.
- You treat the network as code. You write automation yourself (Python or similar), and you've built or run the pipelines, source of truth and telemetry that make that safe.
- You've owned availability for something that couldn't go down, and can walk us through a real incident: what broke, how you found it, and what you changed.
- AI-native in how you work. You've built with these tools, not just used them, and you have a view on where they help in operations and where they don't.
- You think like an owner. You bring ideas, not tickets, and you want to help build a team, not just a network.
- A clear, direct communicator who's comfortable with partners' engineers and with our founders.
Nice to have
- Experience at an internet exchange, or running peering at scale.
- Open networking stacks like SONiC, OcNOS or FRR, or contributions to them.
- Streaming telemetry (gNMI/gRPC, sFlow), and building your own monitoring tooling.
- 400G/800G and optical (ZR) deployments, including vendor selection and certification.
- Access networks (GPON/XGS-PON) and MikroTik or Huawei gear, since many partner ISPs run it.
- Building networks in emerging markets such as Africa or Latin America.
- DDoS mitigation at the edge.
If you don't tick every box but have built and run large networks in production, apply anyway.
Compensation & Benefits
Competitive salary and meaningful equity in a venture-backed company (US-incorporated, with a Kenya operating entity)

About Stora
Stora is building the operating platform for modern self-storage businesses.
Our software helps operators manage bookings, payments, customers, facilities and day-to-day operations from one place, while automating much of the work that traditionally makes running a self-storage business unnecessarily complicated.
In just over five years, Stora has grown from an early-stage product into a platform used by more than 500 operators.
We’re a product-led, remote-first company with an experienced engineering team and ambitious plans for what comes next.
Now, as the engineering organisation grows, we’re hiring an Engineering Manager to make sure the way we lead, develop and support engineers grows with it.
The Role
This is a genuine people leadership role.
You’ll manage approximately 12 engineers working across three product teams, with the team expected to continue growing.
Each product team has a Tech Lead responsible for technical direction, alongside Product and Design. Your focus is different: the engineers themselves.
This isn’t a role for somebody looking to move away from engineering completely, though. You’ll need enough technical depth to understand the work, follow engineering discussions and ask good questions without needing to be the person making every technical decision.
You’ll work closely with our Head of Engineering and have support from People, but you’ll have meaningful autonomy to improve how engineering management works at Stora.
What Else You’ll Own
Engineering Management
- Manage engineers across multiple product teams through regular, useful 1:1s, coaching and clear feedback.
- Make expectations clear and help engineers understand what good performance looks like.
- Identify performance issues early and handle difficult conversations properly when needed.
- Support engineers in progressing from junior through senior and beyond.
- Build strong relationships with engineers without creating unnecessary management overhead.
Performance & Progression
- Own the engineering performance and progression approach.
- Review and improve our existing career levels, expectations and review processes.
- Make promotion and progression decisions that are consistent, evidence-based and understood by the team.
- Create a culture where feedback happens throughout the year rather than being saved for formal reviews.
Hiring & Team Development
- Own engineering hiring alongside the relevant Tech Leads and wider team.
- Help define what we need before a search begins, assess candidates properly and maintain a high hiring bar.
- Ensure new engineers have a structured and useful onboarding experience.
- Think proactively about team composition, capability gaps and future hiring needs.
Team Health
- Pay attention to engagement, retention, collaboration and emerging people issues across the engineering organisation.
- Work with Tech Leads when team problems sit somewhere between technical delivery, behaviour and team dynamics.
- Help maintain a strong remote engineering culture as Stora grows.
Technical Context
- Stay close enough to the engineering work to understand what the team is solving and the environment they’re working within.
- Be comfortable reading code, following pull requests and participating intelligently in technical conversations.
- Partner with Tech Leads without competing with them for technical ownership.
What Success Looks Like
After your first year, we’d expect:
- Engineers to have a clear understanding of what is expected of them and how they can progress.
- Managers and engineers to be having better, more useful conversations about performance and development.
- Performance issues to be addressed early rather than becoming surprises.
- A progression framework that works for the engineering organisation Stora has become, not the company we were several years ago.
- Stronger and more consistent hiring and onboarding.
- The Head of Engineering spending less time acting as the default people manager for the entire engineering organisation.
What We’re Looking For
We’re looking for an experienced Engineering Manager, rather than somebody taking their first step into management.
You’ll ideally have:
- Previous experience directly managing software engineers across more than one team or product area.
- A strong track record of developing engineers at different stages of their careers.
- Hands-on experience managing performance, including difficult or underperformance situations.
- Experience making promotion and progression decisions.
- Experience running or improving engineering career frameworks, review cycles or progression processes.
- Previous experience hiring software engineers and building effective interview processes.
- An engineering background that allows you to understand code and contribute meaningfully to technical conversations.
- The judgement to know when to get involved and when to leave technical decisions with the Tech Leads.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, particularly in a remote environment.
- A practical understanding of how AI tools are changing software engineering and experience using them in your own work.
Experience with Ruby or Rails would be useful, but it isn’t essential.
We’re much more interested in whether you can lead engineers well.
What This Role Isn’t
It’s worth being clear that this isn’t:
- a Tech Lead role with some people management added on;
- a delivery or project management position;
- a Product Manager role;
- a hands-on engineering role where you’ll spend most of your week writing production code;
- a first Engineering Manager opportunity.
Technical leadership already exists within the product teams.
We’re hiring you because engineering management itself deserves dedicated ownership.
Our Technology
You won’t be expected to spend most of your time writing production code, but you should be comfortable working around our stack.
Backend: Rails, PostgreSQL, Redis, Sidekiq, TimescaleDB
Frontend: Turbo, React, ViewComponents, Sass
Testing: Minitest, Playwright
Deployment: GitHub Actions, Heroku
Salary & Benefits
- Salary: Highly competitive and depending on experience
- Location: Fully remote within the UK or Ireland
- Belfast office: Available for anyone who wants to use it
- Private health insurance for you and your family
- Company pension
- 35 days’ annual leave inclusive of applicable public/statutory holidays, depending on location
- Learning and development support
- Share options
- Work-from-home budget
Our Hiring Process
We’re reviewing applications as they arrive rather than waiting for a closing date.
If your experience looks like a strong match, we’ll explain the process clearly from the outset and move quickly.
EQUAL OPPORTUNITIES AT STORA
Stora is an equal opportunities employer.c
We want to build a workplace where people are treated fairly, with dignity and respect, and where different backgrounds, experiences and perspectives are valued.

- An initial intro call with a Talent Partner
- An interview with the Hiring Manager

At Primer, the right challenge comes with the right support: strong onboarding, a collaborative environment, and a team that is genuinely invested in your success. It's never something you face alone.

About StackOne
StackOne is the integration infrastructure for AI agents. Backed by GV and Workday Ventures ($24M raised), we make it possible for any AI agent — whether our customers build it into their product or buy it off the shelf — to take real action across the enterprise stack. Our platform gives agents 560+ connectors and 35,000+ pre-built actions, an AI connector builder for everything not covered yet, and the production layer agents actually need: semantic tool discovery that cuts token use by up to 80%, managed authentication and per-action permissions, the most accurate prompt injection defense on the market, and end-to-end observability.
Join us on our fast trajectory to build the future of agentic integrations.
ROLE
Own ARR and pipeline targets as an Account Executive at StackOne, driving revenue growth in agentic integrations, one of the fastest-moving areas of B2B AI. You'll own the UK-EU territory — a market where StackOne already has customers, brand, and momentum — and run it with a high degree of autonomy.
Full-cycle sales ownership across inbound and outbound, selling to our three ICPs and closing flagship UK-EU accounts. You'll partner async with our US-based CEO and Founding GTM on strategy and deals, while working from our London office (min 2 days a week) alongside our CTO and the product and engineering team. If you want a territory to own rather than a playbook to follow, this is it.
WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING
- Own UK-EU revenue and pipeline targets tied directly to closed ARR.
- Run full-cycle sales across inbound (PLG-driven developer traction) and outbound motions.
- Sell to three ICPs: AI-native startups building agents, enterprise teams embedding AI into existing products, and SaaS platforms embedding StackOne for their customers.
- Execute and iterate on the UK-EU outbound motion (account targeting, messaging, sequencing, experimentation).
- Run live product demos independently and speak credibly about APIs, MCP, and integration architecture.
- Partner with pre-sales engineers on deeper technical validation and enterprise security conversations.
- Collaborate closely with Product Marketing to refine messaging for technical buyers.
- Help build early UK-EU lighthouse accounts and expansion playbooks.
- Track and report on pipeline health, deal velocity, forecasting accuracy, and win rates.
QUALIFICATIONS
- 2–5 years of B2B SaaS closing experience with clear evidence of overperformance and rapid progression.
- Strong track record of owning revenue targets, not just supporting deals.
- Experience in early-stage or fast-growing startup environments.
- Experience selling dev tools, APIs, infrastructure, or other highly technical products.
- Comfortable selling to engineers, CTOs, and technical founders, and running demos independently.
- Exposure to AI/LLM products, agentic platforms, or meaningful hands-on experience with AI tools.
- High ownership mindset, bias for action, and comfort operating with autonomy — your GTM partners are US-based, so you'll run your patch without daily oversight.
Nice to have: iPaaS/integrations background, security/compliance exposure (SOC 2, HIPAA), experience selling alongside PLG motions.
Dealbreaker: pure enterprise sales background with no exposure to startup environments.
BENEFITS
- Join one of Europe's fastest-growing startups.
- Work alongside an experienced team, with backgrounds from Google, Microsoft, Oracle, Coinbase, JP Morgan, and more
- Meaningful share options (EMI) — share in the company's success as we grow.
- Flexible hours and hybrid working — some flexibility in start and finish times, with 2 days minimum in our London office (come in more if you prefer!)
- 25 days holiday + 1 additional day per year of tenure.
- Private health insurance — including dental & optical.
- £15/day lunch budget when working from our London office, up to £180/month.
- £1,000 for your home office setup + £500/year top-up.
- Health, fitness and gift card discounts.
- Cycle2Work and Electric Cars scheme.
- Annual team offsites to sunny spots (last ones were in Croatia and Portugal ☀️)
Ready to help us change the game for SaaS integrations? Get in touch and let's chat!
We believe diversity drives innovation. We encourage individuals from all backgrounds to apply. As an equal-opportunity employer, we celebrate diversity and are committed to creating an inclusive environment for all employees.
