THE PROBLEM WE'RE OBSESSED WITH
The best analytical work in the world is locked inside human heads and PowerPoint slides. It doesn't compound. It doesn't scale. Every engagement starts from zero.
A market map built this year gets filed away. The judgment a senior consultant develops over a decade; about what questions to ask, where the risks hide, how to structure a narrative; disappears when they move firms. Extraordinary talent. Workflows that haven't changed in twenty years.
Riplo is a software company. We build the operating layer that makes expert analytical work repeatable, scalable, and compounding; starting with private equity diligence, the most rigorous, high-stakes analytical workflow in finance.
We raised $3.1M in pre-seed in December 2025, led by Cherry Ventures, with angels from McKinsey, BCG, QuantumBlack, OpenAI, Goldman Sachs, and Hg Capital.
The category is being defined right now. This role is how we define it.
WHAT YOU WILL DO
- Own the engagement end to end. You lead live AI-enabled diligence engagements; commercial DD, vendor DD, market analysis. You own the output and the client relationship from kickoff to delivery. A PE partner receives a finished product ready to present to their IC. The bar is the same as McKinsey. The timeline is a fraction of it.
- Close the product feedback loop. Every engagement surfaces what the AI got wrong, where the analyst had to intervene, which question the system couldn't answer. You translate that into structured product input that makes the next engagement faster and better. You are the connective tissue between the work and the platform.
- Build the knowledge architecture. A great diligence framework built today should not have to be rebuilt tomorrow. You turn repeatable patterns into building blocks the platform runs autonomously next time. You are not just delivering work. You are codifying expertise into software.
- Contribute to growth. You know what deal partners care about, what makes a good output, and what the alternatives cost. You use that; opening doors, joining early sales conversations, helping build a GTM motion grounded in genuine expertise.
- Everything else that matters. At this stage, the job changes week to week. What stays constant: you are in the room for every critical decision, and you co-own what follows.
THE MINDSET
- Obsessed with quality. You know what great diligence looks like. You hold the work to the standard you learned in consulting; and you are energised by the challenge of making AI match it, then exceed it.
- Systems thinker. You ask: why did this take as long as it did? Where did the process break down? What would make it ten times faster? You see the workflow underneath the work and you build to fix it.
- Owner, not executor. You do not wait for specs. You see what needs to happen and you make it happen; client deliverable, product improvement, or commercial conversation nobody else is having.
- AI-native, not AI-curious. You use modern tools to move faster, know where they add genuine leverage, and care about what actually makes it into a deliverable a client will trust.
- High bar, low ego. You hold yourself to a standard higher than what is asked. You seek feedback, close loops, and when someone has a better idea you say so.
WHO YOU ARE
- 3–8 years at MBB or equivalent; at Consultant to Senior Manager level, with meaningful PE diligence experience in commercial DD, vendor DD, or technology DD.
- Software and tech services sector experience is a strong plus. Direct exposure to AI in a PE context; AI portfolio work, technology DD, or AI strategy for funds or portcos; is the sweet spot.
- You have exceptional analytical horsepower; even by the standards of top consulting. You are genuinely interested in AI, ideally with evidence of it: professional usage, side projects, etc.
- You are motivated by the startup opportunity, not just the role. You are comfortable with ambiguity, fluid priorities, and working without a playbook. You are low ego, eager to learn, and team-oriented; someone who makes the people around them better.
- We do not care about pedigree for its own sake. We care about what you have actually done and how fast you learn.
WHY THIS JOB, WHY NOW
Most people who are right for this role are good at their current job. On track. The path ahead is clear. This is not that path.
This is the moment before the category exists; when the decisions you make about how AI-native diligence should work will be the ones the industry copies in five years.
You will be in client meetings, product debates, and commercial conversations that would take a decade to reach at a larger firm. The founding team ran the engagements at McKinsey, BCG, DeepMind, and Hg. We are not building a product about diligence. We are rebuilding it from the inside.
If you want to do the best work of your career and have it actually matter; this is the role.
WHAT WE OFFER
- Competitive salary and meaningful equity from day one
- More context, responsibility, and impact than people with far more senior titles at larger firms
- Direct daily access to founders who have built and backed category-defining companies
- The chance to define what AI-native diligence looks like; from inside the engagements, not a deck about it
If this is the problem you want to work on, we want to hear from you.

ABOUT PLANE
Plane's mission is to build the infrastructure the world's work runs on. Every organization runs on three things: the projects it's driving, the knowledge it keeps, and the requests it fields. Plane brings all three into one open, adaptable platform: simple enough for any team to adopt, dependable enough for organizations to build on. And we are building it for a future where humans and AI agents do that work together.
Plane began in public on GitHub at the end of 2022. Since then it has grown into a work management platform used by teams around the world: 55,000+ stars, 5,000+ forks, and a contributor community that reads our code and files our issues. Organizations run Plane as a managed Cloud service, on their own infrastructure, or inside fully isolated environments. Building in the open keeps us close to users and raises the standard for everything we ship.
Plane is the #1 work infrastructure in aerospace, defense, financial services, and other regulated industries: organizations whose requirements for control, auditability, and data residency rule most software out. When the strictest buyers pick a system of record, that choice means something. Adoption is growing fastest on Plane Cloud and in sovereign clouds, deployments that keep everything inside a country's own borders and rules.
Plane is backed by top investors and built across San Francisco, London, and Hyderabad. We work in tightly knit teams, stay close to users, and care about the visible product as much as the unglamorous details that make software dependable. People own problems end to end, and we add process only when it helps the work.
HUMANS AND AGENTS
We believe the next decade of work will be done by humans and AI agents together. Not agents replacing people, and not a chat window bolted onto software built for humans clicking around, but both working in one system of action, where an agent's work is as visible and as accountable as a person's.
Most software treats AI as a feature. We treat agents as a kind of worker, and that changes what the system underneath has to be. Agents are only as good as the context they can see and the state they are allowed to change, so shared context, explicit state, durable history, and accountable action are not items on our roadmap. They are the product. Plane is built so that when an agent acts, the humans responsible can see what happened, why, and on whose authority, and the record survives.
This is what the infrastructure is for: making the future where humans and agents work together useful, legible, and fully within the organization's control. Every role at Plane is some part of building that.
ABOUT THE ROLE
Plane has over a million users, and Fortune 500 companies deploying Plane. Enterprises in aerospace, defense, healthcare, and finance are running Plane in production — some in air-gapped, classified environments. The commercial demand is real and growing. This role exists to own it.
You'll run full-cycle enterprise deals from first conversation to signed contract. You'll work directly with the CEO and the product team, because at this stage, a deal isn't just a sales process — it's a product feedback loop. You'll sell into technical buyers who already know the product, navigate complex procurement in regulated industries, and help build the playbook as you go.
Plane's sales motion is product-led. The funnel doesn't start with cold outreach — it starts with teams already using Plane and hitting a ceiling where they need enterprise capabilities: compliance, SSO, air-gapped deployment, priority support. Your job is to convert that organic interest into expanding enterprise revenue.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
Run deals end-to-end — from first enterprise inquiry to signed contract. You own the entire arc: discovery, demo, technical evaluation, security review, procurement, negotiation, close. Full-cycle means full ownership.
Convert product-led interest into enterprise revenue — Plane's funnel doesn't start with outbound. It starts with someone self-hosting Plane, hitting a scale or compliance ceiling, and raising their hand. Your job is to recognize those signals, engage at the right moment, and guide the conversation from "we're evaluating" to "we're deploying."
Navigate complex enterprise procurement — our buyers sit in aerospace, defense, healthcare, and finance. That means security questionnaires, compliance reviews, legal redlines, multi-stakeholder approval chains, and timelines measured in months, not days. You need to know how to move a deal through that machinery without losing momentum.
Hold technical credibility in the room — you'll be talking to VPs of Engineering, DevOps leads, and IT architects about self-hosted deployments, air-gapped environments, SSO configurations, and data residency requirements. You don't need to be an engineer, but you need to hold your own in these conversations and know when to bring one in.
Build and refine the sales playbook — document what works. Which objections come up repeatedly? What's the typical deal cycle? Where do deals stall? What collateral is missing? You're not just selling — you're creating the system that the next 3-5 AEs will run on.
Feed product with deal intelligence — every deal you run generates signal about what the market wants, what competitors are doing, and where Plane has gaps. You bring that signal back to the product team in a structured, actionable way — not as a feature request list, but as a pattern.
WHAT YOU'LL BRING
- You've closed enterprise software deals in the $500K–$1M ACV range, running the full cycle yourself — not inheriting qualified pipeline from a BDR team or handing off to a solutions engineer for the technical conversation.
- You've sold into technical buyers — engineering leadership, DevOps, IT — and you can have a real conversation about deployment models, infrastructure, and security without reading from a script. You understand the difference between selling to someone who writes code
and selling to someone who writes checks.
- You've worked at an early-stage company (Series A or earlier) where the sales infrastructure didn't exist yet. You've built your own pipeline, written your own sequences, created your own collateral, and figured out the motion before it was documented.
- You understand product-led growth and know how to work with it rather than against it. You don't fight the free tier — you see it as the top of your funnel and know how to identify when a user is ready for an enterprise conversation.
- You're comfortable with long deal cycles and multi-stakeholder procurement processes. You don't get rattled when a deal takes 4 months and involves legal, security, compliance, and IT all having veto power.
- You're structured in how you manage your pipeline, your notes, and your follow-ups. Not because someone made you use a CRM, but because you've learned that rigor is what separates someone who closes from someone who's "always about to close."

ABOUT THE ROLE
Engineers at Signal AI are expected to bring a strong product mindset to their work. They’re comfortable with complex problems and proactively look for ambiguous ones rather than wait for others to resolve them, and work wherever the product needs them across the full stack. Engineers work closely with other disciplines, including applied research and design, as part of teams that own revenue-critical products from ideation through to production.
Owning a product end to end means much of an engineer’s time goes on understanding the problem: talking to colleagues in research, design and product, testing assumptions, and deciding what is worth building.
Our engineering teams are organised around the needs of the business. We value collaboration and teamwork, and we believe the best solutions to complex problems come from working together. You will work primarily within a small cross-functional team, contributing to its architecture and to engineering standards. You will provide clear, focused technical plans for current and future solutions, and you will keep the long-term technical vision in view.
AI-assisted development is part of everyday work across the organisation. We expect engineers to use tools like Claude Code to move quickly across the entire software development lifecycle, so more of their time is spent on the product questions that matter.
WHAT YOU’LL BE DOING
- Building intuitive user interfaces and data visualisations that unlock valuable insights for our customers.
- Building services that can cope with large volumes of data.
- Implementing and maintaining the AWS infrastructure that supports the services owned by the team.

- Building observability into everything you ship (logging, metrics, alerting).

- Communicating with other teams and stakeholders when needed.
- Working in a collaborative environment. Pairing for most of your time, giving and receiving reviews, and helping to uphold the team’s shared quality standard.
WORKING WITH AI
This is not specifically an AI Engineer role, but every senior engineer in this team is expected to be AI-literate, in two directions: using AI to build better, and building AI into the product responsibly.
- Keep your practice current. Use current models, coding agents and agent tooling in your daily work, and re-test earlier assumptions as capabilities change; what was unreliable six months ago may be routine today.
- Open mind, evidence-led. Give a new tool, pattern or model a fair chance and evaluate it against our own codebases and workflows before ruling it out. Push back when something is presented as a silver bullet and adopting it would bring more risk, or more change, than the team can absorb. Make both calls on evidence, not on instinct or hype.
- Quality bar parity. Agent-generated code and content are held to the same standard as human work. Review it, test it and secure it the same way.
- Build to learn. A working prototype in front of a Product owner or a customer beats a slide. Be as willing to report a disappointing result as an exciting one, and kill weak ideas early.
- Design the human checkpoints and watch the cost. For agentic features, define what the system may decide alone, what needs approval and what escalates, and keep token and run costs visible alongside the value delivered.
- Share what you learn. Contribute to how the team adopts AI across the whole lifecycle (planning, review, testing and release, not only coding) and share your findings with the team and the wider P&T group, so practice spreads beyond one person.

We want you to apply for this position. We want people to enjoy a good experience at Signal AI and we appreciate your professional needs might be different to what we can offer.

- Versatile Skill Set: We value versatility and the ability to work on both back-end and front-end development, and across two product domains. If you are passionate about expanding your skills across different areas, you'll find this role enriching and fulfilling.
- Collaborative Communication: Our culture emphasises building strong communication paths with various teams and stakeholders, including the Editorial team that depends on our tooling every day. If you enjoy collaborative problem-solving and sharing insights, you'll fit right in.
- Team-Oriented Programming: We encourage pair programming and team collaboration over solo work. If you find joy in teamwork and learning from peers, you'll thrive here.
- Flexible Coding Approaches: While we respect the discipline of TDD, we also appreciate flexible and innovative approaches to coding, and we prioritise observability over exhaustive test coverage. If you're open to experimenting with different methodologies, this role offers a great opportunity to broaden your horizons.
- Leveraging AI: We're not just building AI products; we use AI to build better. We expect our engineers to actively explore and adopt AI tools that make them more productive, and to keep their critical thinking switched on while doing it.
- Owning Our Systems: When something goes wrong in production, we don't point fingers. We fix it, learn from it, and improve our observability to catch it earlier next time.
If these aspects align with your professional values and aspirations, we believe you'll find a rewarding career with us at Signal AI.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/runway-ml/9a9f687a-6d61.description_excerpt:
We are building AI to simulate the world through merging art and science.
We believe that world models are at the frontier of progress in artificial intelligence. Language models alone won’t solve the world’s hardest problems – robotics, disease, scientific discovery. Real progress requires models that experience the world and learn from their mistakes, the same way that humans do. And this kind of trial and error can be massively accelerated when done in simulation, rather than in the real world.
World models offer the most clear path to general-purpose simulation, changing how stories are told, how scientific progress is made and how the next frontiers of humanity are reached.
Our team consists of creative, open minded, caring and ambitious people who are determined to change the world. We aspire to continuously build impossible things and our ability to do so relies on building an incredible team. If you are driven to do the same, we'd love to hear from you.
*Titles posted to our careers page are updated regularly to best advertise the role and expected seniority, but internally we have a flat titling system with two types of titles: one for individual contributors and one for people managers.
ABOUT THE ROLE
Open to hiring remote across North America and London — we also have offices in NYC, San Francisco, Seattle, and London.
We're building a tool that makes content creation easy and accessible for all types of creatives. Our users love it. Runway has an actively engaged and growing community of passionate artists and creators worldwide. And we're scaling the systems behind our support team so we can keep delivering delightful experiences as that community grows.
We're looking for a Support Systems Engineer who ships production code, not tickets and specs: someone who takes a fix from proposal to merged PR themselves. This role reports directly to the Head of Customer Experience.
WHAT YOU’LL DO
- Own the AI support agent, our ticketing system and other Support tools end to end: authentication (JWT), response logic, routing, escalation paths and tone, tested in staging before it sees live traffic
- Ship daily product changes that remove ticket volume. Recent example: extending automatic refund eligibility to one-click credit purchases, accidental upgrades and month-based proration on annual terms
- Build and maintain internal CX tooling as real software, not one-offs: scripts, jobs, dashboards, admin surfaces
- Run QA and evals with real test suites and pass/fail rubrics, plus monitoring and alerts for outages, bugs and volume spikes
- Own releases: staged rollouts, a regression suite before every ship, clear rollback criteria, a writeup when something reaches production
- Build the CX reporting the org runs on: volume, deflection, CSAT, reply and resolution time, escalation accuracy, agent spend. You own the correctness and availability of the queries.
- Build and stage the guardrails on refunds, account changes and anything touching money or PII, including the audit trail
- Keep the knowledge base accurate and structured for the agent to parse, and manage the handoff into the ticketing system
- Keep the CX roadmap and the coverage model current, sequenced against priorities set by the Head of CX, so gaps show up before they bite
- Run the day-to-day with our AI platform vendor: weekly working session, joint roadmap, issues filed with reproductions
- Carry signal across teams: Product and Engineering on bugs and rollouts, Customer Education on self-serve, community on Discord and the forums, GTM and Analytics on routing and reporting
WHAT YOU’LL NEED
- 5+ years in Customer Experience, Support Engineering or Support Operations, with real time spent writing code
- You ship production code in codebases you didn't write: read TypeScript, trace logic through someone else's service, put up a PR that survives review. Our stack is TypeScript and Node.js on AWS
- Hands-on experience building and tuning AI or LLM-powered support workflows: prompt and context engineering, routing, escalation design, evals
- SQL experience. You own the reporting, so you shouldn't be waiting on Analytics for it
- Code-level experience with a billing or payments API: invoices, prorations, refunds. A large share of consumer tickets live here
- Git, PR review, CI, staging and feature flags as your default way of working
- Real QA and eval experience: you can define rubrics, build test suites and calibrate against what good looks like
- Judgment about where a fix belongs, in code, in the agent or in the knowledge base
- A track record carrying signal between support, product and other functions and turning it into action
- Comfort managing your own work in a fast-moving environment, high ownership and high autonomy
- Genuine interest in AI, creative tools or both
WHAT SETS YOU APART
The most successful person in this role treats the agent and the systems around it like a product they own. They watch where it fails, ship the fix and check whether it worked. They build reporting people actually use. And they show up with improvements no one asked for yet.
FOR YOUR APPLICATION
During our interview process, you'll have several chances to get acquainted with the Runway product and use all the features our team has built, and that starts now. As part of your application, instead of a cover letter, we ask that you try out the Runway product, specifically build a custom workflow.

There are many factors that go into salary determinations, including relevant experience, skill level and qualifications assessed during the interview process, and maintaining internal equity with peers on the team. The range shared below is a general expectation for the function as posted, but we are also open to considering candidates who may be more or less experienced than outlined in the job description. In this case, we will communicate any updates in the expected salary range.
Lastly, the provided range is the expected salary for candidates in the U.S. Outside of those regions, there may be a change in the range, which again, will be communicated to candidates.

WHAT IS SYLVERA ANYWAY? ‍👩‍👨🌳
Sylvera helps organisations make confident decisions in carbon and commodity markets. We independently assess the quality of carbon projects, track market pricing and supply signals, and provide geospatial and carbon intensity data — giving our clients the clarity they need to invest in real climate action.
We're a team of 130+ scientists, engineers, and market experts based across London, New York, São Paulo, Singapore, and Tokyo. Our work spans market intelligence, geospatial analytics, multi-scale lidar research, and policy analysis. We partner with governments and policymakers to raise the bar for transparency and rigour across carbon markets.
Backed by over $96 million from investors including Fidelity, Balderton Capital, Index Ventures, and Insight Partners, we're trusted by Fortune 500 companies, major financial institutions, and governments worldwide.
If you care about climate, enjoy solving hard problems, and want to work with people who take the mission seriously — we'd love to hear from you.
What will I be doing? ‍‍👩‍💻👨‍💻‍‍
Having found an early product-market fit in a nascent, rapidly growing space, we’re scaling our Ratings Team at pace to support our carbon data platform. We’re looking for a mission-driven analyst to conduct carbon project assessments and help build our expert assessment frameworks ensuring that everything we do is built on robust and comprehensive data and analysis. It’s a critical role at the heart of our business - you’ll work within a large team of multidisciplinary analysts, working together to leverage all the skills and insights necessary to drive value for our customers. You will report to our Nature-Based Solutions Lead.
Specific responsibilities will include:
- Conducting carbon project assessments, providing deep due diligence on carbon projects focussed on providing value to the customer through timely and robust data and insights
- Conduct quantitative and qualitative research, such as assessing project documentation, scientific literature, news reports, modelling formulas, time series data, and geospatial data
- Contributing toward process improvement initiatives and the design of systems and tooling to improve the speed and quality of our assessments
- Collaborate with stakeholders across the business, notably in technology, data, product, commercial teams
- Ensuring that critical quality assurance processes are upheld to maintain our status as the markets most trusted data provider with our carbon project assessments
- Promote and uphold best practices in the team, including keeping customer value at the heart of what we do
We’re looking for someone who: 🧠💚
- Based in London (this role is on-site, with five days a week in our London office)
- Has deep critical thinking skills and the ability to apply logical principles in order to quickly determine actionable solution pathways to complex problems
- Has experience delivering data insights as well as innovating new analytics
- Has established knowledge of quantitative analysis techniques and high familiarity with common quantitative tools for example Sheets, GIS software, SQL, Python, etc.
- Excellent English written communication and collaboration skills
- Fast learner, self-starter, intellectually curious, quantitative and ready to get up-to-speed in a complex and technical domain
- Takes initiative, excellent time-management skills, and adapts easily to change especially when operating toward deadlines
- Is a self-starter who thrives in constantly evolving environments, ideally with early-stage experience
- Cares deeply about the climate and ecosystems of the Earth
- Additional language skills in Spanish, Portuguese or Japanese are advantageous
- We’d like someone highly ambitious, motivated and eager to propel their career forward. We prioritise grit, positivity, and the willingness to get stuck in, and encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't exactly match this job description
Benefits 💰
- Equity in a rapidly growing startup
- Private Health Insurance and Life Assurance
- Unlimited annual leave - and encouragement to actually use it!
- Enhanced parental leave
- Up to 20 days paid sick leave
- No corners cut in having the best tech to do your job
- Access to Mental Health support
- Monthly team socials
Location 🌍
- London, Old Street.
Our values 🙌
- Own it: We make new mistakes. We build on the momentum of our wins and reflect on and learn from our failures.
- Stay curious: We take a growth mindset to our work, our customers, our market and the opportunities ahead of us.
- Do what’s right - even when it’s hard: We keep our focus on the long-term, even if that means short-term challenges.
- Collaborate with empathy: Our teams deliver through active collaboration. We invest in each others’ success and make the company stronger in the long-run.
- Empower Customers - Make extraordinary efforts to exceed our customer expectations. If we’re serving our customers to the fullest, we can help direct more investment into real climate impact.
What if you’re a partial fit? 🌱
We prioritise grit and positivity and encourage you to apply even if your experience doesn't exactly match this job description.
Equal employment opportunity 🌈
Sylvera is an equal opportunity employer: we value diversity. We do not discriminate on the basis of race, religion, colour, national origin, gender, sexual orientation, age, marital status, veteran status, or disability status.
AI note-takers 🤖
We sometimes use AI note-takers to help us transcribe interview notes, so we can be more present in your interview. If you'd like to opt out of us using automatic transcribers, please note this in the free text field in your application, otherwise we'll take your application as confirmation that you're happy for us to use notetakers (whether added to video calls or in the background).

jobs.ashbyhq.com/seccl/873545b0-a001-4aa.description_excerpt:
Hybrid working with two/three days a week in our Edinburgh office, depending on ‘in-office’ support required that week.
ABOUT US
Seccl is the Octopus-owned embedded investment platform, on a mission to help more people invest, and invest well.
We’re building the infrastructure behind the next generation of investing. Our technology already powers some of the UK’s most ambitious fintechs, banks, financial advisers and wealth firms, with close to a million investors relying on Seccl-powered platforms. And we’re now expanding into Europe.
We’ve got a proven product, strong momentum and big ambitions for what comes next: helping more household-name brands launch and scale investment propositions, entering new markets and replacing outdated investment infrastructure with technology that’s faster, simpler and built for scale.

Seccl and Octopus are both B Corp certified and share a belief that profit and purpose should go hand in hand.
If you want to help shape the future of investing in the UK and across Europe, you’ll be in good company.
Check out the Seccl website https://seccl.tech/ to see what we’re building and read more about our mission https://seccl.tech/about/ to shape the future of investments.
THE ROLE
We’re looking for a Junior IT support analyst to join our TechOps team, reporting to the Senior IT support analyst. This role will help us deliver outstanding IT support to Seccl staff as we continue to scale.
Our TechOps team sits within Engineering and underpins Seccl’s modern workplace. It’s a fast moving, collaborative environment with plenty of variety, from supporting joiners, movers and leavers, to managing the Mac device lifecycle and SaaS admin. You’ll quickly build hands on experience with the latest tech.
WHAT YOU’LL OWN
- Act as the first point of contact for internal IT queries, owning triage and providing first contact resolution where possible
- Meet first response SLAs and keep colleagues updated on ticket progress through clear, friendly communication
- Support the joiner / mover / leaver process, from equipment provisioning and account setup to access changes and deactivation, maintaining an accurate IT asset register
- Keep endpoints compliant with our security standards in a Mac first environment
- Use our ticketing tools (e.g., Jira Service Management) and suggest pragmatic improvements to workflows and automation
- Be a friendly face for TechOps, especially on busy office days - helping new starters settle in and resolving day-to-day issues quickly
THIS ROLE’S FOR YOU IF...
- You’re proficient with Mac and comfortable supporting colleagues in a Mac based environment (essential)
- You have a strong interest in technology, a problem solving mindset and clear, empathetic communication (essential)
- You’re organised, proactive, friendly and confident engaging with people across the business (essential)
- You’re happy to work 2–3 days a week from our Edinburgh office to support colleagues in person (essential)
- You’ve had exposure to Microsoft 365 - Azure AD, Entra, Outlook, SharePoint, OneDrive (desirable)
- You’ve used Jamf or other endpoint management (e.g., Intune) and understand the basics (desirable)
- You’ve used Jira Service Management or similar ticketing systems and/or the Atlassian suite (desirable)
THIS ROLE ISN’T FOR YOU IF...
- You’re less comfortable in people-facing roles. As the first port of call for IT issues, and one of the first faces employees meet as they join Seccl, strong people skills are essential!
- You’re not comfortable working in a fast-paced environment. Our speed and scalability are what set us apart; you need to be able to act quickly and think on your feet
- You struggle to follow through on ideas. We value people who do what they say they will. If you care about something, you have the freedom here to make it happen
- You don’t like change. You’ll get on great here if you relish the ambiguity of rapid growth and are willing to embrace uncertainty
WHAT’S IN IT FOR YOU
We offer a generous mix of benefits designed around the things that matter to our people:
- 💰 £27,000 - £30,000, reviewed annually, plus a 6% employer pension contribution and life assurance
- 🌴 27 days’ holiday plus bank holidays, your birthday off and paid dependant leave
- 💙 Two volunteering days each year
- 🌎 The option to work abroad for up to six weeks a year
- 🌟 Secclbrate, our recognition programme offering flexible rewards including extra pay, additional holiday and increased learning budget
- 🏅 One-month paid sabbatical after eight years
- 🏥 Private medical insurance with AXA Health
- 👪 Enhanced parental leave
- 💻 MacBook and up to £500 towards your home office set-up
- 📖 £750 annual learning budget
- 🌻 Health and wellbeing support, including free therapy through Wellness Cloud and mental health support through Headspace
- 🌱 Financial wellbeing benefits, including Octopus Money, the Octopus Share Incentive Plan and will writing through Octopus Legacy

OUR CULTURE
We put people first and try hard to create an environment where people feel trusted, heard and able to do their best work.
We value openness, curiosity and different perspectives. You’ll have the freedom to challenge how things are done, experiment with better ways of working and take real ownership of your impact.
Check out our Glassdoor page for the latest reviews or our LinkedIn for company updates and insights from the team.
INTERVIEW PROCESS
Interviewing is a two-way process. Our interviews are conversational, with plenty of time for you to get to know us and ask questions too:

EVERYONE’S WELCOME
We want to build a diverse and inclusive company full of brilliant people with different skills, experiences and perspectives. All applicants will be considered without regard to age, ethnicity, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, family or parental status, national origin, veteran status, neurodiversity or disability.
If this sounds like your kind of thing, we encourage you to apply even if you don’t tick every box. We’d love to hear from you.

jobs.ashbyhq.com/thaleron/cf8c484e-f6ea-.description_excerpt:
Who Are We?
Thaleron is a seed-stage startup with a big goal, to make a carbon-free grid drastically cheaper than fossil fuels. There are three core foundations to achieving this - generation, storage and transmission.
We were originally founded to develop an entirely new mechanical energy storage technology. We have proven it in the lab, and are now building our first scale prototypes.
More recently, we've been working on the other foundation that is ripe for innovation, transmission. The DC transmission grid is central to large-scale renewable energy deployment, and the technologies and operating principles will significantly differ from traditional AC systems.
What You'll Do:
- Design high-voltage AC/DC converters with custom topologies and control strategies.
- Simulate and validate designs using PLECS, LTspice, MATLAB/Simulink, or similar tools.
- Build early-stage prototypes and test systems—own the bench as much as the whiteboard.
- Write real-time embedded firmware for converter control (microcontrollers or DSPs).
- Design and tune control loops, switching strategies, and fault-handling logic.
- Solve practical challenges in insulation, EMI, thermal management, and safety.
- Work at the intersection of hardware, firmware, and physics to create something truly original.
What We're Looking For:
- Degree in Electrical Engineering or related field, with experience in both power and embedded systems.
- Strong foundation in circuit theory and converter-level design
- Hands-on experience building and testing power electronics hardware.
- Proficient in embedded C/C++ for control systems, ideally with real-time constraints.
- Comfortable working in a fast-paced, low-structure R&D environment.
- Most importantly: a first-principles mindset and the drive to invent, not just optimize.
Why This Is Different
- This isn’t iteration or integration—we’re developing a new power architecture from scratch.
- You’ll be part of a small, deeply technical team where your decisions shape the product.
- We care about real engineering—not just specs, but how and why things work.
- You’ll build hardware that directly impacts the future of energy storage and grid resilience.
Candidate Journey:
1. Talent Screen - video call (30-45 minutes) - an introductory call with our talent consultant.
2. Technical Interview - video call (60 minutes) - initial, technically focused interview with our founders.
3. Onsite meeting (120 - 180 minutes) - in-person meeting with the team in Maidenhead. You'll participate in a collaborative task and spend valuable time with the whole team.
This process is designed to give you every chance to get the measure of us, and us of you. The various stages give you a fair opportunity to show your unique strengths and qualities, and enables each of us to establish if we’re a good fit for the other.
Please share with us any individual needs or reasonable adjustments we may need to make in advance of commencing the interview process with us.

- Reporting & Hierarchy: Ensure reporting for management, statutory aligned with latest accounting standards and structure in line with how the business is set up.
- Optimising Business Processes: Review all existing business processes and recommend new ways to do things, reducing complexity, automating manual workflows and driving improvements with AI lead change.
- Enablement & Best Practices: Produce clear technical playbooks, end-user documentation, training initiatives, actively participate in the Workday.
- Community to leverage best practices and influence product roadmaps.
- Integrations: Ensure current integrations are compliant and improved upon.
- Future Projects: new shares tool, integration for other banking partners, updating security user groups, consolidating payroll providers and new FP&A tool.
- Security & Compliance: Enforce strict segregation of duties processes, system audit trails, to ensure audit readiness, and compliant integrations and renewals.
- Application Management: Oversee the ongoing maintenance, vendor relationships, and SLA for all 3rd-party system integrators.
REQUIREMENTS
Essential
- Workday Financial knowledge and experience, including WD expenses module, integrations for Banks, FX and others.
- Engineering excellence, coding, processing understanding and redesigning.
- Someone who enjoys collaborating across various teams within Finance and the wider organisation including the People Team, Engineering, Security and others.
- Systems implementation, configuration, development and support.
- Business process analysis and a flexible approach with a willingness to constructively challenge existing practices.
- A passion for providing an excellent end-user experience and automation.
- AI-Curious: understand how to prompt LLMs, use APIs, and excited about deploying AI agents to replace repetitive human processes.
- Self-motivating and at home in a fast-paced and rapidly-changing environment with competing deadlines.
- Build strong relationships with internal and external stakeholders to deliver desired outcomes for the team and organisation.
- Advanced Excel, database and programming.
Desirable
- Accounting knowledge, maybe someone who is a Part Qualified or Qualified Finance professional.
- Experience in a Systems role in an SME enterprise.
- Worked within the software SaaS industry previously.
We actively hire candidates who demonstrate technical excellence in their field and welcome people of all ages and backgrounds, providing everyone with equal access to professional development. You are encouraged to apply even if your experience doesn't accurately match the job description. We also encourage applications from those with different abilities, including candidates with ADHD, autism, dyslexia or dyspraxia.

Our product helps security teams quickly and accurately detect intrusions in their cloud environment using canaries - decoy tripwires deployed to deceive attackers.
We're at a massive inflection point and this is a hugely exciting time to join the company:
- We've just raised a $20m Series A https://tracebit.com/blog/series-a led by FirstMark with Accel, MMC, Tapestry and CCL.
- We doubled ARR last quarter, work with companies like Riot Games, Docker and Snyk, and have grown from 5 people to 26 in 18 months.
- Our research https://www.techradar.com/pro/security/google-gemini-security-flaw-could-have-let-anyone-access-systems-or-run-code recently helped fix a P1 security flaw in Google's Gemini CLI.
We’re looking for an experienced engineer who…
- Cares deeply about producing high quality work and is ready to dig into the details but is savvy in making the correct tradeoffs on pace vs. quality.
- Has spent 7+ years shipping software at some degree of scale and/or criticality.
- At a Product focused company and/or working with at least 1 of the public clouds (AWS, Azure, GCP, etc.)
- Is excited by the pace and rate of change that is inevitable in any successful, early stage startup.
- Gets their energy from getting things done and in the hands of customers but is also here to have fun along the way!
If you don’t fit this bill exactly but think you could make a difference here - please, apply!
Role
Reporting to Niall https://www.linkedin.com/in/niall-gallagher/, our Engineering Lead, and with significant exposure to our CTO and Co-Founder, Sam https://www.linkedin.com/in/sam-j-cox/, you’ll join a team of other awesome engineers looking to make their mark on the world.
This includes:
- Working face to face with both founders, the whole engineering team and our customers and prospects to build a delightful product that solves real problems.
- Working across the stack, mostly in C# on .NET Core 10 (here's why https://tracebit.com/blog/why-tracebit-is-written-in-c-sharp), but also Terraform and building out our frontend in HTMX.
- All the good practices you’d expect from technical co-founders who’ve done this before (CD, Infrastructure as code, simple but scalable and powerful architecture)
- We’re a small, tight team with demanding customers so expect to be shipping every day with very little bureaucracy.
- We actively encourage AI-assisted development and give every engineer full access to tools like Claude and Codex.
- We’re based in a Central London office and work here 5 days a week (and everyone we hire will too).
FAQS
How is work organised at Tracebit?
It’s a small, tight team - we have a standup everyday, each team member is usually responsible for delivering something reasonably large for customers and we meet every few weeks to talk about longer term plans. Between that - there’s a tonne of discussions, customer feedback and analysis, but not a huge amount of process, the team is trusted to prioritise where to spend their time.
Where is the office?
The whole team works together in an office right next to Warren Street tube station https://tfl.gov.uk/hub/stop/940gzzluwrr/warren-street-underground-station/ - there are lots of great places to grab lunch nearby.
Are you doing hybrid/remote?
‍Short answer: No, but flexible on a day to day basis.
Long answer: We are set on building the company on a foundation of an office based culture. We are a very early stage company and think that we’ll build the best company at the fastest pace we can whilst also having a lot of fun by physically working together 5 days a week. On a case by case basis (e.g. leaving early for a holiday, staying home for a builder, working remote for a few days to visit family, etc. etc.) we’re very reasonable and flexible. We respect that this is not for everyone.
‍What are the working hours like?
‍We think 9am-6pm will bring a great cadence to work. As a Founding Engineer there will definitely be times you need to pick up work outside of these hours, we’re keen to limit this where we can but also offer flexibility in return.
Can you sponsor visas?
We can support various types of working visas in the UK, including:
- Skilled Worker Visa (both from within and outside the UK)
- Intra-Company Transfer Visa

jobs.ashbyhq.com/xbowcareers/304f9f4e-47.description_excerpt:
ABOUT XBOW
Build the future of offensive security with XBOW. Attackers are already using AI to move faster than defenders can react—we’re creating the platform that puts security ahead in the arms race. Our AI-powered system autonomously discovers, validates, and even exploits vulnerabilities, giving organizations proof-backed results in hours instead of weeks.
Founded by Oege de Moor, creator of GitHub Copilot, and backed by Sequoia, Altimeter, and other leading investors, XBOW is applying cutting-edge AI to one of the world’s most urgent problems. In just over a year, our AI, built by a world-class AI team and legendary security researchers — has uncovered thousands of real-world zero-days across the software billions rely on, and became the first autonomous system to reach number 1 on HackerOne.
We’re a team of builders, hackers, and researchers who thrive on solving problems others think are impossible. If you want to push the boundaries of AI, reshape how security is done, and join the group defining this new era of defense — we’d love to talk.
YOUR ROLE
We’re looking for a Software Engineer with deep expertise in LLM prompting, orchestration, and software engineering. In this role, you’ll design and implement systems that coordinate large language models with real-world tasks, advancing the intelligence at the heart of our platform. You’ll collaborate with our AI, Engineering and Security teams to create novel prompting strategies, build orchestration layers, and deliver production-ready systems in TypeScript.
This role is for someone who thrives in a fast-moving, research-driven environment and enjoys turning ambiguous ideas into robust, scalable solutions.
WHAT YOU'LL DO
- Build LLM-powered software that actually works, by designing prompt flows and orchestrations that ensures great performance with no false positives.
- Architect and build an AI-powered software stack that is production-grade, testable and maintainable.
- Design and build experiments and evaluation frameworks for performance testing of the system at scale. Conduct data analysis to draw conclusions.
- Collaborate with the rest of the AI team, with security experts, and both frontend and backend developers to create end-to-end systems that work and customers love.
- Own projects end-to-end: from basic ideation and experimentation to deployment and production monitoring.
- Continuously conduct research on how to harness the advancements in LLMs to make our system better and faster.
WHO YOU ARE
- Strong experience with building software around LLMs: prompting, agentic orchestration, fault-tolerance, and integration of LLM parts with hard-coded logic.
- Strong software engineering skills: architecting and building production-grade software that runs reliably and can be maintained.
- Experience with TypeScript or proven ability to learn a new programming language quickly.
- Strong skills in structured and independently-driven problem-solving. Able to work with incomplete information and rapidly testing hypotheses.
- Comfortable with an energetic environment that mixes the fast-paced agile prioritisation of a startup with the curiosity mentality of a research lab.
- Eager to own projects and jump into the deep end, learning as you go. Curious, adaptable and collaborative.
- MSc or equivalent or higher in computer science, math, physics or machine learning.
BONUS IF YOU HAVE
- Prior experience with the security sector, especially involving offensive security and/or applying LLMs in a security context.
- Contributions to open-source software, particularly within applications of or frameworks for LLMs.
- Strong theoretical background, e.g. a Ph.D in machine learning, computer science or math.
- Startup experience and comfort with ambiguity.
WHAT WE OFFER
- Compensation & Equity: Competitive salary and a generous equity package, making you a true owner of the company.
- Career Growth: Shape your role, lead the function, and grow with the company as we redefine cybersecurity.
- Meaningful Work: You will tackle technically complex challenges and play a pivotal role in the growth of our business, working alongside an amazing team and some of the world’s experts to shape how AI transforms cybersecurity.
WHAT ELSE YOU SHOULD KNOW
- Location: Remote (all team members are remote but we meet regularly and you’re supported to travel to collaborate with colleagues in person)
- Contract: Full-time.
- Hiring Process:
1. 45-min introductory chat with our Talent team.
2. 45 minutes with one of our Engineering Leads.
3. 2-3 hour technical deep dive around relevant case study.
4. 30-min final meeting with the Engineering Lead for the assigned team.
We believe in people who are driven by curiosity and a willingness to learn. Even if you don't check every box, we encourage you to apply if you're excited about the role and our mission.

Working closely with colleagues across Sales, Finance, Product, Engineering, Security and People, you’ll make it easy to engage with Legal, keep matters moving and ensure the team has clear visibility of its priorities.

What you’ll do:
Keep Legal connected to the business
- Be a central point of contact for legal requests, gathering relevant information, coordinating priorities with legal counsel and tracking matters through to completion.

Support commercial contracting

- Help develop contract templates, negotiation playbooks and practical guidance that enable the business to handle routine requests efficiently.
Build and run legal operations
- Own the administration of legal intake, matter tracking and contract management systems, keeping records accurate and accessible.
- Implement and improve workflows for contract review, approvals, signatures and document retention.
- Produce useful reporting on legal demand, contract turnaround times, outstanding matters and external legal spend.
- Coordinate external counsel onboarding, engagement administration, invoices and budget tracking.
- Manage legal subscriptions, service providers and associated renewals.
- Identify practical opportunities to automate repetitive tasks and use approved AI tools, with appropriate handling of confidential and sensitive information.
Provide broader paralegal support
- Conduct legal research and prepare initial drafts of internal guidance, correspondence and other documents for counsel review.
- Support corporate housekeeping, governance records and signature processes.
- Help maintain legal policies and coordinate training and internal guidance.
- Coordinate inputs from Legal, Security and other teams on customer due diligence and related documentation.
- Support legal projects as XBOW’s products, operations and international footprint evolve.

Essential
- 8+ years of relevant experience spanning paralegal work and legal operations, including at least 2+ years in-house.

- Practical experience supporting commercial contracts and working within templates, playbooks and approval frameworks.
- A track record of taking ownership of legal processes and improving how a legal team operates.
- Strong organisational skills and attention to detail, with the ability to manage competing priorities and follow matters through.
- Confidence working with business stakeholders and translating legal processes into clear, practical steps.
- Sound judgement about what you can resolve independently and when to involve legal counsel.
- Experience with contract management, electronic signature and workflow tools, and an interest in responsible uses of AI.
Advantageous

Colleagues know when and how to engage Legal. Contracts and requests move forward with clear ownership and fewer avoidable delays. Legal records are reliable, priorities are visible, and the team has more capacity to focus on complex matters as XBOW grows.

job-boards.greenhouse.io/10alabs/jobs/40.description_excerpt:
About 10a Labs: 10a Labs is the safety and threat-intelligence layer trusted by frontier AI labs, AI unicorns, Fortune 10 companies, and leading global technology platforms. Our adversarial red teaming, model evaluations, and intelligence collection enable engineering, safety, and security teams to stay ahead of evolving threats and deploy AI systems safely.

Our client’s team is responsible for identifying and investigating misuses of their products – especially new types of abuse–and creating systems of defence to address them. Part of this team specialises in the latter, and they need additional support to help them monitor abuse on product launches and design and build scaled detection, review, enforcement, and measurement for uncovered risks. This position is a Full-Time (40 hours per week), contract position.

About The Role:

Protection Science Engineering is an interdisciplinary role mixing data science, machine learning, investigation, and policy/protocol development. As a Protection Scientist Engineer within the client team, you will assist in designing and building systems to proactively identify and enforce on abuse on their AI products. This includes ensuring they have robust abuse monitoring in place for new products, sustaining monitoring for existing products, and prototyping and incubating systems of defense against the highest risk harms.  You will also respond to and investigate critical escalations, especially those that are not caught by existing safety systems. This will require developing understanding of the products and data, and working cross-functionally with product, policy, and engineering teams. 

You will need a strong ability to use SQL and python to query, transform, and understand data, and to build and improve prototype detection. An investigative mindset is key, with experience in identifying and enforcing on bad actors (in any industry). A background including data science, machine learning and classification basics, AI, and/or threat investigation is a plus.

This is a remote position, based in London, UK.  The position includes participation in an on-call rotation that will involve resolving urgent escalations outside of normal work hours, for at least 7 consecutive days per quarter. Some detection and investigations may involve exposure to sensitive and distressing content, including sexual, violent, or otherwise-disturbing material. 

In This Role, You Will:

  • Scope and implement abuse monitoring requirements for new product launches.
  • Improve processes to sustain monitoring operations for existing products, including developing approaches to automate monitoring subtasks. 
  • Prototype and mature into production systems of detection, review, and enforcement of abuse for major harms.
  • Work with Product, Policy, Ops, and Investigative teams to understand key risks and how to identify and address them, and with Engineering teams to ensure we have sufficient data and scaled tooling. 

Requirements:

  • Ability to work remotely on GMT and must be geographically located in the UK.
  • Quantitative and coding background , including statistics/metrics and proficiency in python and SQL.
  • Experience in identifying (and ideally enforcing on) bad actors with scaled tooling.
  • Ability to be on-call approximately once a quarter that will involve resolving urgent escalations outside of normal work hours, including occasional evenings and weekends
  • Ability to rapidly context switch across domains, modalities, and abuse areas, to include high severity areas like violent activities and child safety
  • Excited to work in a fast paced, ambiguous, and purposeful space with high impact across users and beyond, and to learn quickly. 

Desired Qualities (but not required):

  • Background in machine learning and classification, especially on novel or poorly understood behaviours.
  • Experience scaling and automating processes, especially with language models.
  • Experience working with scaled labellers or reviewers, particularly at scale.
  • Familiarity with one of the following topics/areas: AI safety, child safety, abuse by nation state and other malicious actors, digital mental health, fraud abuse, radicalization/persuasion/grooming; hateful activities and groups.

job-boards.greenhouse.io/apothecom/jobs/.description_excerpt:
About ApotheCom

ApotheCom is an exciting leader in the field of medical communications. Drawn together from several backgrounds including the pharmaceutical industry, research, marketing, medical and regulatory writing, sales, publishing, digital media and design, we have the experience and all-round ability to conceive and deliver the best quality medical communications programs.

About the role

The Associate Medical Director is a scientific and strategic lead responsible for the quality, accuracy and strategic direction of assigned medical communications workstreams and accounts.

 

In this role, you will be accountable for ensuring that scientific content is clinically accurate, strategically aligned, insight-driven and relevant to client medical strategy and agency objectives. You will partner closely with client services, editorial, creative, digital, medical writing and senior scientific leadership to ensure that deliverables meet client expectations, reflect current scientific evidence and support broader communication goals.

 

The Associate Medical Director serves as a key scientific contact for clients, faculty and external experts, bringing subject matter expertise, sound judgment and a proactive consultative approach to assigned projects. You will lead and contribute to content development plans, elevate the scientific and strategic quality of deliverables, support new business activity and help guide junior scientific team members.

 

To be considered for this role, candidates should have successfully demonstrated Senior Medical Writer-level capabilities and typically bring at least 5 years of experience in medical communications, publications, medical education or a related scientific communications environment.

 

The Associate Medical Director will report to a Medical Director, Senior Medical Director or senior Scientific Services leader.

 

Key responsibilities

Strategic thinking and scientific insight

  • Accountable for the scientific strategy and quality of assigned accounts, workstreams and deliverables, ensuring alignment with client medical strategy and agency objectives.
  • Leads and contributes to content development plans, ensuring deliverables are grounded in evidence and aligned with strategic imperatives.
  • Interprets and synthesizes complex clinical data, including clinical trial results, congress updates, treatment guidelines, publications and competitive information.
  • Translates complex scientific and clinical information into clear, compelling and strategically relevant medical communications.
  • Provides proactive scientific input into publication plans, medical education programs, communication platforms and other client deliverables.
  • Identifies key scientific insights, evidence gaps and communication opportunities that can strengthen client strategy.
  • Participates in new business pitches, proposals and client onboarding by providing scientific insight and therapeutic area expertise.

Client partnership and excellence in delivery

  • Serves as a key scientific contact for clients, faculty, authors, investigators and external experts, building relationships based on scientific credibility, responsiveness and delivery excellence.
  • Partners with pharmaceutical and biotechnology clients to understand goals, communication objectives, scientific priorities and success measures.
  • Reviews and elevates scientific content to ensure not only accuracy, but also strategic alignment with client objectives.
  • Ensures assigned medical communications are clinically relevant, current and reflective of recent advances in the therapeutic area.
  • Liaises with clients and external experts to support streamlined, efficient development of high-quality deliverables.
  • Supports the planning and execution of advisory boards, investigator meetings, faculty meetings, congress activities and scientific workshops.
  • Anticipates client needs, flags risks early and recommends solutions to protect scientific quality, timelines and budget expectations.

Teamwork, collaboration and leadership

  • Partners with Client Services and cross-functional colleagues across creative, digital, editorial, account and specialized services to ensure deliverables meet client expectations.
  • Provides day-to-day scientific direction to medical writers, freelancers and junior scientific team members.
  • Offers formal and informal mentorship, coaching and performance feedback to junior team members, supporting their scientific growth and delivery quality.
  • Demonstrates increasing autonomy in account decision-making while knowing when to escalate scientific, client, budget or delivery risks.
  • Proactively drives team growth and efficiency, including suggestions for process improvement within the team, cluster or squad.
  • Contributes to key strategic priorities, including recruitment, resourcing, business development and operational excellence.
  • Collaborates with project and account teams to ensure timelines are realistic, scope is understood and scientific requirements are appropriately planned.

Content development and quality oversight

  • Leads or oversees development of scientific content across manuscripts, abstracts, posters, slide decks, advisory board materials, white papers, monographs, congress materials and medical education content.
  • Reviews and refines medical writing to ensure scientific accuracy, strategic relevance, logical flow, appropriate tone and audience fit.
  • Conducts targeted literature reviews and evidence assessments to ensure content reflects current clinical practice and therapeutic developments.
  • Maintains awareness of good publication practices and appropriate standards for publications, medical education and professional communications.
  • Provides quality control for scientific content developed by internal writers, freelancers and external partners.
  • Ensures reference support, data interpretation, claims and scientific messaging are accurate, balanced and appropriately substantiated.

Financial and operational awareness

  • Understands the financial side of assigned accounts and works with team members to help projects remain in scope.
  • Provides senior scientific input into scopes of work, budgets, timelines and resource planning.
  • Identifies potential changes in project focus, scientific complexity or scope and escalates appropriately.
  • Supports efficient delivery by balancing scientific excellence with timeline, budget and client-service…

Senior Medical Writer

(Publications or Medical Affairs)

London ,Manchester, Macclesfield, Glasgow, Hybrid or UK remote

 

The power of three of the world's leading medical communications companies – Nucleus Global, ApotheCom and Ashfield MedComms – and the specialised services and skills within MEDiSTRAVA combine to form iNIZIO Medical. With over 2,000 employees globally, iNIZIO Medical creates compelling content and engage communities across the spectrum of healthcare. We improve scientific understanding and pioneer new ways of partnership, with a united vision to lead and define the future of medical in drug development and commercialisation.

Due to continuing growth within iNIZIO Medical we have some fantastic opportunities to join our teams across Nucleus Global, ApotheCom and Ashfield MedComms.

We are looking for a Senior Medical Writer with opportunities across multiple therapy areas.

This role would suit an experienced Senior Medical Writer. It will provide a great career development opportunity for you with the support of a very experienced team.

Reporting to a Scientific Director, you will develop scientific expertise in assigned therapeutic areas, supporting delivery for a versatile team. Core deliverable tasks include researching and developing technical materials, ensuring that a candidate or employee makes all outputs follow written brief, makes them accurate in content and editorial style, and references them. You will also communicate with clients and KOL on content development and attend scientific meetings.

To succeed you will have:

· Several years experience working within a medical communications agency environment.

· An academic background in the life sciences (Bachelor of Science, Master of Science, Doctor of Philosophy)

 

We offer a great compensation package including pension, life insurance, private healthcare and paid time off. In addition to our benefits package, we are happy to talk flexible working with hybrid and remote working options available. We offer excellent opportunities for career and personal development, including opportunities to transfer your skills to our other agencies globally.

Our Pledge

We are committed to promoting a culture of diversity, inclusion and belonging where everyone can bring each facet of themselves to work each day. We believe that strength in diversity and inclusivity is a driver of our success. We strive to accelerate the adoption and adherence of new medicines across the globe. We're determined to advance scientific understanding and pursue health equity for all. Inizio Medical is part of Inizio, a strategic partner for health and life sciences with a full suite of medical, marketing, advisory and engagement services.

Don't meet every job requirement? That's okay! Our company is dedicated to building a diverse, inclusive, and authentic workplace. If you're excited about this role, but your experience doesn't perfectly fit every qualification, we encourage you to apply anyway. You may be just the right person for this role or others.

Engineered Arts is the leading manufacturer of full-size humanoid robots used for entertainment, education and communication. With 20 years of hardware and software development, our robots have been sold in over 30 countries worldwide with customers such as NASA, PwC, Meta and many more.

Why You'll Love This Job

Coupa, SAP S/4HANA: Procurement and AP, SAP Ariba Buying / Invoicing, Oracle Fusion/EBS, Workday, NetSuite, Sage, etc.) to lead onboarding for new customers and drive their implementation of our product. - Fantastic communication and documentation skills
- Extreme attention to detail and pride yourself in being incredibly proactive

- You’re able to push back and still make people happy
- Very comfortable with software configuration (not necessarily technical skills, which would be a plus)
PERKS & BENEFITS
At Zip, we’re committed to providing our employees with everything they need to do their best work.
- 📈 Start-up equity
- 🦷 Health, vision & dental coverage
- Commuter benefit
- 🌴 Flexible PTO
- 💻 Apple equipment plus home office stipend
- 5% Employer Pension Contribution

We look forward to hearing from you!

Allow us to introduce ourselves

Hello there! We’re Appinio, a global market research company that combines an AI-powered insights platform with expert consultancy. On a mission to make the world a little more fact-based, we help companies understand how consumers think and make smarter decisions.

We started out in Hamburg back in 2014, but we’re now humbled to call the world our playground, with over 260 employees spread across 13 countries (we’re remote-first), 2600+ international clients, delivering research from +190 markets, globally.

Want to be a part of the Appinio movement? 🚀

Here at Appinio, we value transparency in our recruitment process, and we've created a blog to share what to expect during each step of our journey together: here

Your mission as a Sales Development Representative

We are looking for a Sales Development Representative to to serve as the critical bridge between Marketing and Sales. In this role, you will focus on the top of the sales funnel by building outbound pipelines, managing inbound channels, and qualifying leads through initial discovery calls. 

What you’ll be doing

  • You serve the critical bridge between marketing and sales, focusing entirely on the top of the sales funnel
  • Proactively build a high-quality outbound pipeline, identifying and approaching new prospects within your target market and contact prospects
  • Filtering and contacting leads who have interacted with marketing content, the platform or masterclasses. Following up on event registrations. Managing the lead funnel
  • Management of our inbound channels
  • Conducting initial discovery calls to identify the potential client’s issues, their market research requirements and budget, as well as their organisational structure.
  • CRM management: Document all interactions and track data clearly within our HubSpot environment.

You will thrive in this role if

  • You have 2+ years of experience as a SDR, BDR or similar in B2B sales, ideally within the Market Research industry, and understand how to translate insights into value
  • You’re a hungry, proactive hunter who enjoys taking ownership of your pipeline and driving results
  • You have a consultative, empathetic mindset, skilled at understanding client needs and building meaningful relationships
  • You’re organised, analytical, and data-driven, using structure and insights to guide decisions and improve performance
  • You have a creative, can-do attitude and are able to think outside the box
  • You’re naturally curious, coachable, and eager to learn, always looking to grow your commercial skills
  • You thrive in a collaborative, international environment, contributing to shared goals and an open feedback culture
  • You are fluent in both German and English (written and spoken)

What’s in it for you?

  • Flexibility Policy - Average is 30 days taken, however, we do not have a hard cap of number of vacation days as we know life happens
  • Temporary work from abroad - If you're based in the EU, you can work outside your country of residence for up to 180 days per year
  • All the hardware you need and your own MacBook
  • If you are located in Hamburg or Berlin, you'll get a Deutschland ticket or access to a mobility budget with the NAVIT app to get you to and from the office space
  • Subsidised Urban Sports Club or ClassPass membership based on location

Overview 

Sales Account Executives at Asset Reality own the full sales cycle with public sector agencies, from first conversation to closed contract. You'll run complex, multi-stakeholder sales processes across agencies where decisions move slowly and budget authority is rarely obvious, requiring the kind of discipline and commercial instinct to keep deals moving to closure.

What this role is 

You’ll be working in a small UK/EU focused team with a mission to convert an expansive public sector market opportunity. Your job is to build relationships of trust to get to the heart of the challenges that government agencies face when it comes to seizing and managing assets, from boats to bitcoin. You will be passionate about understanding their problem, identifying a champion and getting the attention of the economic buyer. You are comfortable owning the whole sales lifecycle, from identifying opportunities, to leading product demos, and closing deals.  

This is a role for someone who can run a complex, multi-stakeholder sales process with discipline and patience. Government agencies don’t move fast, and decisions rarely sit with one person. You’ll need to navigate that while keeping commercial momentum. 

  

What you’ll be doing 

  • Learning everything about Asset Reality, our solutions, our clients and the problems we can help them solve and how we do it better than any other combination of solutions  
  • Generating your own pipeline, where needed, through direct outreach and event follow-up and nurturing qualified leads referred to you from the team  
  • Running deep discovery to go beyond the initial qualification: understanding how the agency currently works, the real problem, their current risks and full scope of impact  
  • Identifying and navigating to the economic buyer, using your champion and contacts as a route in

Location: London Office/Hybrid (1–2 days on site)
Schedule: Full-Time

 

The Role 

Most security roles protect data. This one protects evidence. Asset Reality builds mission-critical infrastructure for clients in law enforcement and government, operating in environments where records are examined adversarially and the stakes are high. 

You will join a small engineering team as a working engineer with deep security expertise. This is not an advisory role and it is not a governance role. You will ship production code alongside the rest of the team — Go services, Postgres, React, all on AWS — and you will be the person who makes sure that what we ship stands up to adversarial scrutiny. 

Security here is not a separate function reviewing the team's work from the outside. It is a discipline embedded in how the team designs, builds, and operates the product. You will set the standard for that.

 

Responsibilities

  • Contribute to day-to-day product development as a senior engineer: designing, writing, reviewing, and shipping production code in Go and React.
  • Own the security dimension of engineering work: lead threat modelling on new features and architectural changes, drive secure design decisions, and review high-risk changes.
  • Own and improve the security of our AWS estate: IAM design, network segmentation, secrets management, and data isolation in a multi-tenant system.
  • Build security into the development lifecycle: dependency and vulnerability management, CI/CD security controls, static and dynamic analysis, and the tooling that makes the secure path the easy path.
  • Design and build product security features where the domain demands them: audit integrity, tamper evidence, access controls, and data isolation.
  • Lead the technical side of incident response: detection, investigation, and remediation, and the exercises that keep us ready.
  • Support client-facing security work with technical depth: contribute to security questionnaires, due diligence responses, and client assessments where engineering answers are needed.
